title: High-resolution parallel-translation CT reconstruction based on a patch-based adaptive-regularization-guided diffusion model.
abstract: Computed tomography (CT) is an effective technique for industrial non-destructive testing (NDT). However, conventional rotational CT is difficult to apply to the scanning and reconstruction of large plate-like objects, while its mechanical system is also relatively complex. In response to these limitations, parallel translation CT (PTCT) has been introduced. Nevertheless, due to its limited scanning range, PTCT acquires incomplete projection data, which leads to aliasing artifacts and makes accurate reconstruction challenging. To address these issues and achieve high-resolution PTCT reconstruction, this paper proposes a patch-based adaptive-regularization-guided diffusion model. Specifically, an initial estimate obtained by the Simultaneous Iterative Reconstruction Technique (SIRT) is first employed, introducing structural prior information into the reconstruction process. Based on this, a split-and-reassemble denoising module (SRDM) is designed to perform patch-wise reconstruction, where positional encoding is incorporated as conditional guidance to enhance the representation of local structural details. Furthermore, an adaptive-regularization-based correction module (ARCM) is introduced, in which seam-based and mask-based regularization terms are adaptively adjusted according to the denoising stage to support global structural recovery and improve local structural continuity. To evaluate the proposed method, a PCB dataset containing samples with defect structures is constructed. The results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves reliable performance in global reconstruction while effectively recovering fine structural details within defect regions.

title: Exploring the potential of bile fluid dynamics analysis to inform clinical strategies for choledochal cysts: Experimental and numerical studies.
abstract: Surgical intervention is essential for choledochal cysts (CCs) due to their high lifetime risk of progressing to cholangiocarcinoma, yet management strategies vary worldwide. Given bile fluid's vital role in digestion, investigating bile flow dynamics may provide surgeons with additional insights for treatment planning. In this study, one MRI-based healthy adult scan was used to reconstruct biliary system, which was then modified according to Todani classifications to generate eight CC types. Particle Image Velocimetry was used to first visualize local velocity field, followed by computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of bile emptying to analyze pathological non-Newtonian bile flow. Wall shear stress (WSS), a key biomechanical parameter, was visualized through 2D surface mapping for comparative evaluation. Results showed consistently low velocity in dilated regions, suggesting bile accumulation in CCs, particularly in Types 1a, 2, 4a, and 4b. While WSS changes were minimal in the healthy biliary system, extreme gradients, up to 10,000-fold emerged in CCs, especially Types 1a, 2, and 4a. These findings highlight that bile flow characteristics are primarily dictated by localized anatomical abnormalities, aligning with surgical interventions that target dilated regions. These findings demonstrate the potential of CFD to provide additional biomechanical insights into bile flow abnormalities associated with different CC types, which may serve as a reference for future clinical investigations.

title: Adversarial robustness of deep learning-based thyroid nodule segmentation in ultrasound.
abstract: Deep learning-based segmentation models are increasingly integrated into clinical imaging workflows, yet their robustness to adversarial perturbations remains incompletely characterized, particularly for ultrasound images. We evaluated adversarial attacks and inference-time defenses for thyroid nodule segmentation in B-mode ultrasound. Two black-box adversarial attacks were developed: (1) Structured Speckle Amplification Attack (SSAA), which injects boundary-targeted noise, and (2) Frequency-Domain Ultrasound Attack (FDUA), which applies bandpass-filtered phase perturbations in the Fourier domain. Three inference-time mitigations were evaluated on adversarial images: randomized preprocessing with test-time augmentation, deterministic input denoising, and stochastic ensemble inference with consistency-aware aggregation. Experiments were conducted on a U-Net segmentation model trained on cine-clips from a database of 192 thyroid nodules. The baseline model achieved a mean Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.76 (SD 0.20) on unperturbed images. SSAA reduced DSC by 0.29 (SD 0.20), from 0.76 to 0.47, while maintaining high visual similarity (SSIM = 0.94). FDUA resulted in a smaller DSC reduction of 0.11 (SD 0.09), from 0.76 to 0.65, with lower visual fidelity (SSIM = 0.82). Against SSAA, all three defenses significantly improved DSC after correction, with deterministic denoising showing the largest recovery (+0.10, p < 0.001), followed by randomized preprocessing (+0.09, p < 0.001), and stochastic ensemble inference (+0.08, p = 0.002). No defense achieved statistically significant improvement against FDUA, although recall consistently improved at the cost of reduced precision. The tested inference-time defenses therefore partially mitigated spatial-domain perturbations, whereas statistically significant DSC recovery was not demonstrated against frequency-domain perturbations, highlighting attack-specific challenges in adversarial robustness evaluation.

title: Multivariate cortical thickness-cognition covariance supports the criterion validity of the Riga Cognitive Screening Task.
abstract: There is a predicted increase in the prevalence of older adults presenting with mild to severe cognitive impairment. Screening tools with high sensitivity are the first frontier in identifying a cognitive pathology; however, to ensure that they are measuring the intended concept or criterion, thorough psychometric procedures should be followed. In this study, concurrent criterion validity of Riga Cognitive Screening Task was measured, using cortical thickness of regions of interest as the criterion. 106 older adults (Mage = 70.49, SD = 8.08, 35.8% male) with varying levels of cognitive functioning were involved in the study. All participants underwent cognitive assessment with the screening task and a 3T MRI. Cortical thickness of selected temporal and parietal regions was used as a brain measure. Behavioural Partial Least Squares Correlation was conducted and one latent variable was extracted. The results confirmed that Riga Cognitive Screening Task shows good criterion validity, suggesting successful use for screening.

title: Stabilization of canine ilial body fractures using an anatomically contoured locking iliac plate: A short retrospective case series.
abstract: Objective To report the clinical outcomes of canine ilial body fractures stabilized with a newly designed, anatomically 3.5 mm Steelvet Iliac Locking Plate. Study design Retrospective case series. Animals Ten client-owned dogs treated between 2023 and 2024. Methods Medical records and orthogonal pelvic radiographs were reviewed for signalment, fracture configuration, surgical findings, time to radiographic union, postoperative sacral index (SI), complications, and limb function. Continuous variables were summarized as median (interquartile range, IQR), mean ± standard deviation (SD), and range; categorical variables as counts and proportions with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results Median age was 3.5 years (IQR 2.25-5.75; range 0.75-10) and median body weight 32.0 kg (IQR 28.3-38.5; range 21-52). Median time to radiographic union was 60 days (IQR 60-62.5; range 60-97). Six of ten dogs (60%; 95% CI 31.3-83.2%) achieved union by 60 days. One dog (10%; 95% CI 1.8-40.4%) developed a cutaneous fistula that resolved within seven days of plate removal after fracture healing. The SI was within normal limits in all dogs at final follow-up, and limb function was normal in 10/10 dogs. Conclusions In this small case series, stabilization of canine ilial body fractures with the dedicated 3.5 mm Steelvet Iliac Locking Plate was associated with reliable bone healing, a low complication rate, and preserved pelvic canal dimensions. Clinical significance: A dedicated, anatomically contoured locking plate is a feasible option for fixation of canine ilial body fractures, conforming to the iliac surface with no or minimal intraoperative contouring and allowing straightforward application. Larger comparative studies are warranted.

title: Enhancing medical image segmentation with HCE-Net: A heterogeneous feature collaborative extraction network.
abstract: Medical image segmentation occupies a pivotal role in clinical diagnosis and therapeutic planning. Conventional segmentation techniques struggle to accommodate the intricate representational attributes of medical images, while prevailing deep learning segmentation models predominantly adopt homogeneous single encoders and linear feature fusion paradigms, thereby exhibiting inherent limitations in contextual modeling, fine-grained feature excavation, and contour segmentation accuracy. To address such dilemmas, this paper proposes a Heterogeneous Collaborative Feature Extraction Network (HCE-Net). Establishing a dual-path heterogeneous encoding architecture, this network excavates complementary feature representations in a parallel manner. An Orthogonal Fusion Module (OFM) is elaborately devised to integrate Sobel edge priors with multi-scale convolutions, enabling the precise capture of edge and contour characteristics. A Diversified Receptive Field Module (DFM) is constructed to consolidate multi-scale detail manifestations and preserve global contextual cues. Furthermore, Adaptive Aggregation Connection (AAC) is embedded within skip connection branches to supplant conventional simplistic concatenation, efficaciously mitigating the technical bottleneck of heterogeneous feature fusion. Comparative experiments conducted on three publicly accessible medical datasets, encompassing dental radiographs, pulmonary CT scans, and retinal vascular images, demonstrate that HCE-Net substantially elevates segmentation accuracy, enhances boundary integrity, and ameliorates the general robustness of the model. It manifests distinguished application prospects across diverse medical image segmentation scenarios.

title: Robust sex differences in regional gray matter volume but shared personality-gray matter associations in young adults.
abstract: Relationships between personality traits and brain regions have been widely studied, but potential sex-based differences have received less attention, despite sex hormones affecting neuronal activity and brain functions. We aimed to determine whether the personality-brain relationship differs fundamentally between the sexes. We enrolled healthy university students (103 men, 111 women). Gray matter volumes were measured in 388 brain regions using voxel-based morphometry on T1-weighted brain MRI, and personality traits were assessed using the temperament and character inventory. In confirmatory analyses correcting for multiple comparisons across all 388 regions and seven factors (Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate), main-effect sex differences in gray matter volume were robust: 17 regions survived correction, independent of personality, and were predominantly subcortical (thalamus, pallidum and putamen) and right-lateralized. By contrast, neither any association between personality and gray matter volume nor any personality-by-sex interaction survived correction, indicating that personality-gray matter associations were not detectably different between the sexes. In a cross-validated penalized regression over all regions, only self-transcendence was predicted above chance (out-of-sample R2 ≈ 0.04, permutation p = 0.004), and this prediction was essentially unchanged after adjustment for sex and total intracranial volume. In exploratory region-wise analyses (uncorrected p < 0.05), the distribution of brain regions associated with each personality factor appeared to differ between the sexes; for instance, harm avoidance in females was related mainly to parietal, temporal and thalamic regions, whereas in males it was related mainly to sensorimotor and cerebellar regions. These exploratory patterns did not survive correction and are reported as hypothesis-generating observations. Overall, sex differences in this young adult sample were robust for subcortical volume but not for the coupling between personality and gray matter volume, which appeared largely shared between the sexes, underscoring the importance of considering sex as a biological variable while distinguishing confirmed effects from exploratory observations.

title: MoViT-Eye model: A robust and explainable AI-driven approach for automated multi-class ocular disease diagnosis.
abstract: Ocular diseases, including Diabetic Retinopathy (DR), Glaucoma, Pterygium, and Retinal Detachment, require early detection to prevent irreversible blindness. However, manual screening is labor-intensive, and standard deep learning models often fail to capture the complex global spatial relationships necessary for multipathology grading. To address these limitations, we propose a MobileNetV2-Transformer Hybrid (MoViT-Eye) architecture for the automated 5-class classification of fundus images. This framework integrates the efficient local spatial feature extraction of MobileNetV2 with the long-range dependency modeling of Transformers. The study uses 4,906 cleaned images and applies LIME, Grad-CAM++, and Saliency Maps to identify image regions that influence each prediction. These methods generate heatmaps that highlight important clinical features, including microaneurysms and optic disc abnormalities, and support transparent clinical decision-making. The proposed model significantly outperforms existing architectures, achieving an accuracy of 90.36%, a Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) of 0.8643, a Cohen's Kappa of 0.8640, and a specificity of 97.29%. The model achieved an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 98.60% for identifying DR and Retinal Detachment. By combining hybrid feature learning with multi-layered interpretability, this model provides a robust and transparent tool for automated clinical ophthalmic screening.

title: Assessment of algorithmic performance in PET-CT segmentation of solitary lung tumors.
abstract: Background PET-CT (Positron emission tomography-computed tomography), a nuclear medicine imaging technique is preferably used for lung tumor detection. However, manual image analysis may be time-consuming. To enhance efficiency, many automated segmentation algorithms have been developed. This study aims to develop a radiomics agreement-based method to evaluate segmentation algorithms and to compare the performance of two deep learning-based algorithms nnU-Net (No-new-net Convolutional Neural Network) and RECOMIA (Research Consortium for Medical Image Analysis Lung Cancer "Lung Cancer FDG-PET/CT v1.5") for PET-CT solitary lung tumor segmentation. Methods and results PET-CT images of 221 patients at the University of Debrecen's Hospital were collected and anonymized. The predictions of segmented lung tumors done by nnU-Net and RECOMIA were compared with the manual segmented masks via Wilcoxon signed-rank test and Pearson correlation values, based on eight groups of radiomics parameters calculated by PyRadiomics software. The combined p-values were calculated using Brown's method, which were 0.481 and < 0.001 for nnU-Net and RECOMIA, respectively. The absolute values of correlation were summed, which were 37.259 and 16.358 for nnU-Net and RECOMIA, respectively. Altogether, RECOMIA shows statistically greater differences, therefore, it performs worse than nnU-Net does. Statistical analyses with Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), Multivariate analysis of variance (MANOVA) and follow up pairwise t-test further confirmed stronger agreement between extracted radiomics features from nnU-Net predicted masks and manual masks than RECOMIA and manual masks, which validated the proposed comparison method. Conclusion The superior performance of nnU-Net highlights the importance of training data alignment and model adaptability in achieving accurate and reliable segmentation in medical imaging. However, nnU-Net requirements for training and extra computational demands may limit its application in some clinical environments. Despite lower accuracy, RECOMIA remains valuable because of its efficiency and intuitiveness. These findings provide valuable guidance for selecting segmentation algorithms in real-world clinical and research settings.

title: Slice-based YOLO-SAM hybrid prompting framework for automatic medical image segmentation.
abstract: Accurate medical image segmentation is essential for computer-aided diagnosis, treatment planning, and quantitative image analysis. This study evaluates a slice-based automatic segmentation framework that couples YOLOv8-based region localization with prompt-driven Segment Anything Model (SAM) segmentation. In contrast to a simple YOLOv8 + SAM cascade using only bounding-box prompts, the proposed framework adds hybrid prompt generation with bounding boxes and positive/negative points, parameter-efficient fine-tuning of the SAM prompt encoder and mask decoder, and lightweight post-processing. The framework is evaluated on two public datasets under explicitly defined local protocols: 2D slice-based prostate MRI segmentation using Prostate158 and skin lesion segmentation using an internal ISIC 2018 split. On Prostate158, the method obtains Dice coefficients of 89.2%, 76.8%, and 65.3% for central gland, peripheral zone, and prostate cancer lesion segmentation, respectively. On the local ISIC 2018 split, it obtains a Dice coefficient of 94.8% and a Jaccard index of 91.5%. These results indicate competitive performance under the implemented experimental protocol, but they should not be interpreted as protocol-independent state-of-the-art claims. The manuscript clarifies the evaluation unit, prompt-source protocol, 2D processing strategy, hyperparameter settings, baseline grouping, and limitations related to statistical uncertainty, detector failure propagation, and clinical translation.

title: Clinical outcomes after fully visualized transforaminal endoscopic spine surgery in patients with lumbar disc herniation stratified by paraspinal muscle degeneration: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Objective To evaluate pain and functional outcomes after fully visualized transforaminal endoscopic spine surgery in patients with lumbar disc herniation (LDH) stratified by preoperative paraspinal muscle degeneration, and to examine whether degeneration grade was associated with 2-year outcomes. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 129 patients with single-level LDH who underwent surgery between December 2021 and December 2023 and had complete preoperative, 1-month, 6-month, and 2-year follow-up data. Two blinded spine surgeons independently graded bilateral multifidus fatty infiltration from 0 to 4 on axial T2-weighted MRI at the mid-disc level; linearly weighted kappa was 0.967(95% CI, 0.937 to 0.989). Longitudinal outcomes were analyzed using covariate-adjusted patient-level random-intercept mixed-effects models with degeneration grade treated as a categorical factor, followed by adjusted 2-year regression and post hoc sensitivity analyses. Results Of 136 screened patients, 129 were included after excluding 2 with incomplete records and 5 lost to follow-up. The cohort included 64 men and 65 women, with a mean age of 57.36 ± 11.63 years; grades 0-4 included 13, 25, 33, 32 and 26 patients, respectively. All grades improved substantially. In covariate-adjusted mixed models treating grade as a factor, the grade effect was significant for back pain VAS (P < 0.001), leg pain VAS (P = 0.010), and ODI (P < 0.001). The time-by-grade interaction was nominally significant for leg pain VAS (P = 0.036) but not after false-discovery-rate adjustment (q = 0.053), and not significant for back VAS and ODI. Each one-grade increase was associated with higher 2-year back pain VAS (β = 0.114, 95% CI, 0.001 to 0.227, P = 0.048) and ODI (β = 1.001, 95% CI, 0.168 to 1.833, P = 0.019), but not leg pain VAS. Conclusions Fully visualized transforaminal endoscopic spine surgery was associated with substantial pain relief and functional improvement across all multifidus degeneration grades. More severe degeneration showed modest prognostic associations with residual back pain and disability, but the estimated effects were smaller than published minimal clinically important differences. These findings should inform cautious counseling and hypothesis generation rather than be used as a standalone surgical decision rule.

title: Manifold learning and inverse processes for multimodal superresolution in T1 and T2 weighted magnetic resonance imaging.
abstract: We propose a novel multimodal superresolution algorithm based on the analysis of graph Laplacian representations of image data. The algorithm is inspired by a model for heterogeneous data fusion. We demonstrate its application to the problem of magnetic resonance imaging, where superresolution can be used to decrease acquisition times or to improve signal-to-noise ratio. At the core of the proposed algorithm is a joint modality feature matching, performed in the Laplacian eigenmaps embedding space. A sparse L1-regularized preimage reconstruction is then required, in order to produce a high resolution image from its graphical features. To optimize the algorithm's performance, we integrate the spatial information of the image data to improve local correlations. To illustrate the performance of this new method we apply it to the problem of reconstructing high-resolution T1-weighted magnetic resonance images from a combination of high resolution T2-weighted and low resolution T1-weighted images. Our results indicate that the improvement, as compared to conventional single image interpolation schemes, is proportionally greater for low-resolution images. Our results support the use of the manifold learning embedding approach to multimodal superresolution, by demonstrating superior numerical performance over state-of-the-art image superresolution algorithms.

title: Real-time instance segmentation of spine endoscopy images using a YOLO-V11 deep convolutional neural network.
abstract: Background and objectives Spine endoscopic surgery requires precise anatomical recognition and real-time bleeding detection to enhance surgical safety and efficiency. However, most existing computer vision studies do not offer real-time multi-class segmentation of the entire scene. This study aims to develop a real-time instance segmentation model based on YOLO-V11, capable of automatically identifying surgical instruments, critical anatomical structures, and bleeding sites in spine endoscopy. Methods The model was trained and evaluated using 2,181 annotated frames (training 1,741 / validation 216 / held-out test 224) from spine endoscopy images, covering nine key categories: instruments, bone, ligamentum flavum, dura, soft tissue, vessels, fat, the radiofrequency ablation wand, and bleeding focus. The segmentation model's performance was evaluated across various YOLO-V11 variants. Results Across five random seeds per variant on the same NVIDIA A100 GPU, YOLO-V11 l achieved the highest mask mAP50, defined as mean average precision at an intersection-over-union threshold of 0.50, with a value of 0.7735 ± 0.0030 (mean ± SD, n = 5). It also maintained real-time inference, reaching 270 ± 35 frames per second (FPS) with a per-frame latency of 3.75 ± 0.51 ms. All five variants exceeded 30 FPS, the widely accepted real-time threshold for surgical imaging. The model demonstrated high precision in segmenting vital structures such as the dura and ligamentum flavum and accurately identified bleeding regions. Conclusion This research contributes to AI-driven surgical guidance systems, with potential applications in robotic-assisted spine surgery. The developed model enables real-time navigation, improving intraoperative decision-making and enhancing surgical outcomes. In particular, our YOLO-V11-based framework extends prior single-structure or lower-frame-rate multi-element approaches by delivering real-time multi-class instance segmentation of instruments, anatomical structures, and bleeding sites in spine endoscopy, with explicitly quantified inference latency.

title: Pyramid-level training with stain normalization for breast cancer lymph-node metastasis segmentation in whole-slide images.
abstract: Whole-slide histopathology images encode metastatic tissue information simultaneously at multiple spatial scales, from fine cellular morphology at high magnification to broad tissue architecture at low magnification. Existing segmentation models commonly operate at a single fixed resolution, leaving complementary information distributed across the whole-slide image pyramid underused. We present a multilevel segmentation framework with stain-normalization preprocessing that trains a unified model jointly across four study-defined WSI pyramid views (5×-40×), integrating Vahadane stain normalization and structured class-balanced sampling stratified by pyramid level, dataset, and tissue class. Applied to a 280-slide CAMELYON16/CAMELYON17 study cohort under strict slide-level data separation (196 training, 42 validation, 42 held-out test slides), the framework achieves a Dice coefficient of 92.39% on the held-out test set. Relative to the single-scale U-Net baseline (89.00%), the paired slide-level improvement is 3.39 percentage points (95% bootstrap CI: 3.19-3.60 pp; Cohen's dz=4.98; two-sided permutation p < 0.00001). Per-level evaluation confirms that full pyramid fusion outperforms each individual scale, while a boundary-focused L1 audit yields a mean HD95 of 53.88 pixels (95% CI: 50.28-57.64). The contribution is therefore a training-sampling and evaluation pipeline rather than a new network layer or architecture. These results show that multiresolution training, stain normalization, structured sampling, and leakage-controlled evaluation can materially improve breast lymph-node metastasis segmentation on established WSI benchmarks. A supplementary external cross-dataset evaluation on 103 paired BCSS breast-histopathology ROIs, performed without retraining or fine-tuning, yielded a pooled Dice of 70.58%, IoU of 54.54%, precision of 55.95%, and recall of 95.57%; the mean per-ROI Dice was 67.89% (95% bootstrap CI: 65.00-70.76%). These external results demonstrate substantial sensitivity to tumor-like tissue under a different image source and semantic annotation scheme, while also exposing the expected effect of annotation granularity and class-definition mismatch on overlap and boundary metrics.

title: "Pipe-Laying": A novel fusion of 3D MRI and health records for the early detection and diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease using deep learning.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a prevalent form of dementia that impacts brain cells. Although its likelihood increases with age, there is no transitional period between its stages. In order to enhance diagnostic precision, physicians rely on clinical judgments derived from interpreting health data, considering demographics, clinical history, and laboratory results to detect AD at an early stage. While patient cognitive tests and demographic information are primarily presented in text, brain scan images are presented in graphic formats. Researchers typically use different classifiers for each data format and then merge the classifier outcomes to maximize classification accuracy and utilize all patient-related data for the final decision. However, this approach leads to low performance, diminishing predictive abilities and model effectiveness. We propose an innovative approach that combines diverse textual health records (HR) with three-dimensional structural magnetic resonance imaging (3D sMRI) to achieve a similar objective in computer-aided diagnosis, utilizing a novel deep learning technique. Health records, encompassing demographic features like age, gender, apolipoprotein gene, and mini-mental state examination score, are fused with 3D sMRI, enabling a graphic-based deep learning strategy for early AD detection. The fusion of data is accomplished by representing textual information as graphic pipes and integrating them into 3D sMRI, a method referred to as the "pipe-laying" method. This unified approach enables simultaneous processing of textual health records and 3D sMRI data within a single convolutional framework. Experimental results from over 4000 sMRI scans of 780 patients in the AD Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) dataset demonstrate that the pipe-laying method enhances recognition accuracy rates for Early Mild Cognitive Impairment (EMCI) and Late Mild Cognitive Impairment (LMCI) patients, accurately classifying all AD patients. In a 4-class AD diagnosis scenario, encompassing AD, LMCI, EMCI, Cognitively Normal (CN) accuracy improved from 86.87% when only 3D images were used to 90.00% when 3D sMRI and patient health records were included. Thus, the positive impact of combining 3D sMRI with HR on 4-class AD diagnosis was established.

title: Enhancing auto-segmentation accuracy and robustness through multiple deep learning systems.
abstract: Purpose Deep learning auto-segmentation (DLAS) can improve the efficiency and consistency of clinical contouring; however, no single DLAS system performs optimally across all cases, organs, and image slices, and each system may produce occasional poor-quality or outlier contours. Because multiple DLAS systems are available in some institutions, this proof-of-concept study evaluated a multi-system fusion framework designed to leverage their complementary strengths and generate more accurate and robust auto-contours, with potential extension to consensus generation from multiple manual contours. Methods Using 35 abdominal CT datasets from three institutions, contours of the stomach, duodenum, liver, and right kidney were generated by three commercial DLAS systems and one non-commercial research DLAS model. Two fusion approaches were evaluated: conventional Simultaneous Truth and Performance Level Estimation (STAPLE), which combined all available DLAS contours, and a selecting-and-combining DLAS (scDLAS) approach. For scDLAS, previously developed contour quality classification (CQC) models used supervised machine learning and seven quantitative metrics to classify each contour slice as acceptable, requiring minor edits, or requiring major edits. Only contours in the highest available quality category were retained for STAPLE fusion. scDLAS configurations incorporating different numbers of DLAS systems were evaluated against the reference contours using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95), and changes in the distribution of contour-quality categories. Results No individual DLAS system consistently achieved the best performance across all four organs. STAPLE generally matched or outperformed the individual systems while maintaining comparable or lower interpatient variability. For the stomach, duodenum, liver, and right kidney, respectively, STAPLE achieved mean ± SD DSC values of 0.88 ± 0.10, 0.70 ± 0.13, 0.95 ± 0.02, and 0.92 ± 0.04, with corresponding HD95 values of 10.8 ± 12.6, 18.0 ± 12.3, 5.5 ± 2.2, and 6.8 ± 9.6 mm. The best-performing scDLAS configuration increased the mean DSC to 0.90 ± 0.09, 0.74 ± 0.14, 0.96 ± 0.02, and 0.94 ± 0.03, respectively. The highest duodenal DSC was achieved by 3scDLAS, whereas 4scDLAS achieved or tied the highest DSC for the other organs. Conclusion The proposed framework demonstrates the feasibility of leveraging complementary outputs from multiple DLAS systems to improve the accuracy and robustness of auto-segmented contours. These findings support further evaluation of multi-system fusion as a strategy for generating more reliable initial contours for subsequent clinical review and editing.

title: Assessing Condylar hyperplasia management outcomes using semi-automatic segmentation methods: A reliability study.
abstract: Objectives To assess the reliability of two condylar segmentation methods in patients with Unilateral Condylar Hyperplasia (UCH) treated with proportional condylectomy. Methods A sample of 10 patients with UCH who underwent proportional condylectomy was randomly selected from a private practice. Landmarks were defined and volumetric measurements were performed from cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) from affected (n = 10) and non-affected sides (n = 10), as well as before and after proportional condylectomy. Condyles were segmented using two methods: method SN (sigmoid notch method) and method ML (mandibular lingula method). A single blind operator performed the procedure twice, with a four-week interval between the evaluations. Random error was assessed using the Dahlberg formula, and intra-rater reliability was evaluated using the Intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) in a two-way mixed-effects model. Results An excellent reliability was observed for both methods (SN: ICC = 0.96, CI 95% 0.92-0.98; ML: ICC = 0.91, CI 95%, 0.79-0.96). The method ML exhibited a slightly higher variability in measurement agreement, indicating higher random measurement error than method SN. On average, measurements with method ML were 9.9% higher on the second evaluation, while method SN measurements were 4.7% higher. Conclusions Condylar segmentation is a reliable approach for evaluating volumetric changes in complex mandibular condyles. While, both SN and ML segmentation methods demonstrated strong intra-rater reliability, the method SN exhibited slightly lower variability. Nonetheless, this study highlights the potential of method ML as a clinically relevant alternative to condylar assessment.

title: Novel risk models based on screening history results and timing of lung cancer diagnosis: Post hoc analysis of the National Lung Cancer Screening Trial.
abstract: Background Our group previously reported that lung cancer (LC) screening history results and subsequent timing of diagnosis are associated with significant differences in survival outcomes. As a follow-up study, we sought to develop novel personalized risk models that considered screening history for incidence cancers, interval LCs, and prevalence LCs. Methods Using data from the CT-arm of the NLST, four independent case-control analyses were conducted to develop parsimonious risk models. Controls (n = 26,038) were those never diagnosed with LC. The four LC case groups were 270 prevalence LCs, 44 interval LCs, 206 screen-detected LCs (SDLCs) that had a baseline positive screen, and 164 SDLCs that had a baseline negative screen. For each case-control analysis, univariable analyses identified statistically significant covariates from 48 variables and then significant covariates were included into a stepwise backward selection approach to identify a model with the most informative covariates. Model discrimination was quantified by the area under the curve (AUC). Internal validation was performed using 500 bootstrap replications in which the entire variable-selection procedure was repeated, yielding optimism-corrected AUCs, and calibration was assessed using calibration slope and calibration-in-the-large. LASSO logistic regression was applied to all 48 covariates as a sensitivity analysis. Results For prevalence LCs, the model (AUC = 0.711) included age, pack-years smoked, BMI, smoking status, smoking onset age, personal history of cancer, family history of LC, alcohol consumption, and milling occupation. For interval LCs, the model (AUC = 0.734) included age, smoking status, smoking onset age, cigar smoking, marital status, and asbestos occupation. For baseline positive SDLCs, the model (AUC = 0.685) included age, pack-years smoked, BMI, emphysema, chemicals/plastics exposure, and milling occupation. For baseline negative SDLCs, the model (AUC = 0.701) included age, pack-years smoked, BMI, smoking status, emphysema, sarcoidosis, and sandblasting occupation. Optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.676, 0.644, 0.640, and 0.652 for the prevalence, interval, baseline positive SDLC, and baseline negative SDLC models, respectively, and calibration slopes ranged from 0.67 to 0.81. LASSO sensitivity analyses retained largely consistent model covariates. Conclusions Besides smoking and age, which are inclusion criteria for screening, these models identified other risk factors that may inform personalized LC risk assessment. These findings should be regarded as exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

title: Literature Review of the Utility of Ultrasound for Adolescent and Child Ankle Injuries.
abstract: Pediatric posterior ankle pain is a common and challenging presentation due to the complex anatomy and a broad differential diagnosis that includes apophysitis, tendon injuries, fractures, impingement syndromes, infection, and inflammatory arthropathies. Initial evaluation typically consists of physical examination and radiographs, which are often inconclusive and may result in delayed diagnosis, repeat imaging, and/or prolonged immobilization. Magnetic resonance imaging is the gold standard for most of these injuries, but it is expensive and logistically difficult for the pediatric population. A rapid, accessible, and cost-effective imaging modality is needed to improve early detection and management. This review evaluates the role of ultrasound in assessing posterior ankle pathology in pediatric patients. Ultrasound demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy in identifying Achilles tendon tears and differentiating partial- from full-thickness injuries while also assisting in treatment decision making through dynamic tendon gap assessment. It is recommended in several studies for evaluating Achilles tendinopathy and may have predictive value for future symptoms. Emerging evidence supports its adjunctive role in Sever disease and posterior ankle impingement syndrome as well. For osseous and infectious conditions, ultrasound can identify findings suggestive of calcaneal stress fractures, osteomyelitis, septic arthritis, and juvenile idiopathic arthritis. Although magnetic resonance imaging remains the gold standard for these diagnoses, ultrasound improves the detection of joint effusions and synovitis and enhances the accuracy of diagnostic joint aspirations. Overall, ultrasound is a dynamic, radiation-free modality that serves as a powerful adjunctive tool in evaluating pediatric posterior ankle pain.

title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging Morphometric Analysis of the Lumbar Spine and Its Vascular and Muscular Relations: Anatomical Variability and Surgical Planning.
abstract: Background Lumbar region anatomical variability significantly affects the safety of minimally invasive spine (MIS) approaches, yet quantitative patient-specific data remain limited. Objective The primary goal was to characterize vascular, muscular, and skeletal variability in Portuguese patients with lumbar disc disease and assess implications for MIS surgical corridors. A secondary objective was to explore associations between muscle area and disability. Study design Cross-sectional observational study. Methods Lumbar magnetic resonance images from 46 adults were analyzed for vertebral and disc morphometry (L1-S1), psoas and intrinsic back muscles area (at the level of L4-L5 intervertebral disc), psoas-intervertebral disc overlap, psoas-vessel distances (abdominal aorta or the left common iliac artery), and iliac vessel spacing at L5 to S1 (distance between the left common iliac vein and the right common iliac artery). Sex and age were analyzed as comparative and correlational variables. Results Men showed significantly larger muscle areas ( P < 0.001). The ante-psoas corridor narrowed caudally, with L4 to L5 being the most unfavorable level for oblique lateral interbody fusion (32.6% negative overlap). Psoas-vessel distances decreased from L1 to L5 and correlated positively with age. The aortic bifurcation was most frequently located at mid-L4 (50%). Conclusion Marked anatomical variability influences MIS feasibility, particularly at the L4 to L5 level. Individualized preoperative imaging assessment is essential to ensure safe surgical planning and technique selection. Clinical relevance Preoperative MRI assessment of patient-specific lumbar vascular and muscular anatomy may help identify anatomical constraints relevant to minimally invasive lumbar fusion and support individualized surgical approach selection, particularly at the L4-L5 level. Level of evidence: 3

title: Fiducial marker-guided microwave ablation of liver tumors occult on conventional ablation-guidance imaging: A prospective single-center technical feasibility study.
abstract: Backgrounds/aims Some liver tumors are visible on dynamic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) yet remain occult on ultrasound (US), non-enhanced computed tomography (CT), US-CT/MRI fusion imaging, and contrast-enhanced US, which precludes image-guided ablation. We report a prospective single-center feasibility study of percutaneous gold fiducial tagging undertaken to enable microwave ablation (MWA) of such lesions. Methods Of 168 patients (204 lesions) referred for hepatic ablation between January 2024 and March 2025, 25 lesions in 20 patients were occult on all four modalities and were enrolled. A single gold fiducial was implanted under US guidance one day before ablation using MRI-derived anatomic landmarks. Post-placement imaging characterized the three-dimensional fiducial-to-lesion offset and thereby provided a calibrated targeting vector for MWA. Technical success was defined as complete lesion coverage with a ≥ 5 mm circumferential margin on post-procedure imaging. Results All 25 fiducials were placed without complications (median fiducial-to-lesion distance 8 mm, range 2-19). MWA was technically successful in 25 of 25 lesions (100%), and an independently confirmed ≥ 5 mm margin was achieved in every case. No procedure-related complications occurred and no local tumor progression was detected over a median follow-up of 21 months (range 12-30). Conclusions Percutaneous gold fiducial tagging with vector-guided MWA is a feasible and reproducible strategy for ablating liver tumors that are occult on conventional planning modalities, achieving high targeting reproducibility and early local control in a selected cohort.

title: The Vitamin B12-C-Reactive Protein Index in Advanced Cancer: A Case Report and Narrative Review of an Underutilized Potential Prognostic Biomarker.
abstract: Identifying simple, accessible, and reproducible biomarkers that can improve the prognostic assessment of patients with advanced cancer is a major challenge in palliative medicine. The association between vitamin B12 hypervitaminemia and an inflammatory syndrome, as evidenced by elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) levels, could serve as a complementary prognostic biomarker in patients with advanced cancer. Clinical, imaging, and laboratory findings from the reported patient were reviewed. The B12-CRP index (BCI) was calculated as serum vitamin B12 in pmol/L multiplied by CRP in mg/L. Published evidence on elevated vitamin B12, inflammation, and prognostic assessment in advanced cancer was discussed narratively. We report the case of a 64-year-old man with poorly differentiated cholangiocarcinoma diagnosed 5 months prior, treated with gemcitabine-cisplatin in combination with durvalumab. Despite this treatment, a follow-up computed tomography scan revealed major tumor progression with hepatic metastases, portal vein invasion, the development of peritoneal carcinomatosis, and pulmonary nodules. The clinical examination revealed a significant deterioration in the patient's general condition, with a Palliative Performance Scale version 2 (PPSv2) score of 50%. Laboratory results showed hypervitaminemia B12 at 1,126 pmol/L, CRP at 16.8 mg/L, hypoalbuminemia at 30 g/L, significant cholestasis, moderate cytolysis, and hypercalcemia. The BCI was 18,917. Palliative care was required. The BCI could serve as a potential complementary prognostic biomarker to enhance the prognostic assessment of patients with advanced cancer. Prospective studies are nevertheless needed to clarify its role in decision-making strategies in palliative medicine.

title: Prolonged Cholestasis as an Initial Presentation of Miliary Tuberculosis in a Pediatric Patient.
abstract: Miliary tuberculosis is a severe form of tuberculosis resulting from hematogenous dissemination of Mycobacterium tuberculosis and may cause respiratory failure and multiorgan involvement in infants. Hepatic involvement is uncommon and may present as prolonged cholestasis and granulomatous hepatitis, making the diagnosis particularly challenging. We report an infant with miliary tuberculosis presenting with infantile cholestasis and acute respiratory failure. A 2-month-old infant presented with persistent cholestasis developed at 6 weeks of age and acute respiratory failure requiring noninvasive mechanical ventilation. Initial evaluation, including intraoperative cholangiography, excluded biliary atresia, and an extensive infectious, metabolic, autoimmune, immunologic, and genetic evaluation did not identify an alternative cause. Chest computed tomography demonstrated bilateral ground-glass opacities and peripheral micronodules in a miliary pattern. Liver biopsy showed granulomatous hepatitis with focal central necrosis and multinucleated giant cells. The diagnosis of Mycobacterium tuberculosis was confirmed by sputum polymerase chain reaction and acid-fast bacilli culture. A four-drug anti-tuberculosis regimen led to complete clinical, radiological, and biochemical resolution, with full recovery by 4 months of age. Miliary tuberculosis should be considered in infants presenting with severe respiratory failure, prolonged neonatal cholestasis, and granulomatous hepatitis, particularly in endemic regions. Early recognition of miliary pulmonary patterns on imaging and prompt initiation of targeted anti-tuberculosis therapy is critical to improve outcomes and ensure a favorable prognosis.

title: Anterior Pelvic Herniation After Urethral Atresia: A Case Report and the Bladder Space-Occupying Hypothesis.
abstract: We report a case of long-standing acquired urethral atresia in an adult, accompanied by bilateral ureterovaginal fistulas, severe bladder atrophy, and an anterior pelvic hernia. We propose a hypothetical biomechanical explanation to elucidate the possible relationship among these abnormalities. We report a 71-year-old female patient who had undergone urethral tumor resection at another hospital 10 years earlier and had since experienced persistent vaginal urine leakage for more than 10 years; she presented this time with a progressively enlarging vaginal mass. The diagnosis was established based on physical examination, contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT), and intraoperative exploration findings. Intraoperative exploration revealed complete urethral obliteration, bilateral ureterovaginal fistulae, a severely atrophic bladder remnant, and an anterior pelvic hernia containing small bowel that protruded through the vesicouterine fossa and clinically resembled a grade III cystocele. The patient underwent excision of the prolapsed vaginal mass and bilateral cutaneous ureterostomy. Based on the clinical course, imaging findings, and intraoperative observations, a three-stage biomechanical cascade hypothesis is proposed: urethral outlet obstruction may lead to elevated intravesical pressure, which in turn causes "pressure-induced perforation" at the ureterovesical junction. Direct urine diversion through the fistula results in bladder disuse atrophy. Loss of the bladder's space-occupying function leads to reopening of the vesicouterine pouch, which then expands into an anterior pelvic hernia under repeated intra-abdominal pressure. To our knowledge, acquired urethral atresia with bilateral ureterovaginal fistulas in adults has not been previously reported. Although this hypothesis still requires further clinical and finite element modeling studies for precise validation, the proposed "bladder space-occupying effect hypothesis" may provide, in the future, a theoretical framework for subsequent research on atypical pelvic organ prolapse after long-term bladder disuse.

title: A rare injury combination: Hawkins type I talar neck fracture, Jones fracture, and calcaneal avulsion fracture accompanying a bimalleolar ankle fracture.
abstract: Bimalleolar ankle fractures are common traumatic injuries and can usually be identified using standard radiographic examinations. However, associated fractures - particularly non-displaced fractures of the talus and calcaneus - may be overlooked on plain radiographs. Accurate identification of accompanying injuries in complex ankle trauma is of great importance for appropriate treatment planning. In this report, we present a rare case of a bimalleolar ankle fracture accompanied by a Hawkins type I talar neck fracture, a Jones fracture, and a calcaneal avulsion fracture. While the bimalleolar ankle fracture and Jones fracture were detected on initial plain radiographs, the talar neck fracture and calcaneal avulsion fracture were identified only by computed tomography (CT). The bimalleolar ankle fracture, talar neck fracture, and Jones fracture were treated surgically, whereas the calcaneal avulsion fracture was managed conservatively. In ankle trauma, particularly in cases involving multiple fractures, plain radiographs may be insufficient and associated injuries can be overlooked. Talar neck fractures and calcaneal avulsion fractures may not be detected on standard radiographs when they are non-displaced. This case highlights the critical role of advanced imaging modalities, particularly CT, in identifying associated fractures in complex ankle injuries. The use of CT in complex ankle trauma increases diagnostic accuracy and contributes to appropriate treatment planning.

title: Traumatic diaphragmatic injuries from the perspective of thoracic and general surgery: analysis of patient management using the Injury Severity Score (ISS) and Modified Shock Index (MSI).
abstract: Background Traumatic diaphragmatic injury (TDI) is a rare but severe clinical condition associated with high mortality following blunt or penetrating thoracoabdominal trauma. Due to concomitant injuries, the diagnosis of traumatic diaphragmatic injury remains challenging and may be easily overlooked. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnosis and surgical management of traumatic diaphragmatic injuries through a retrospective analysis conducted at a single center between 2016 and 2024. Methods Data from 41 patients who underwent surgical treatment for TDI between 2016 and 2024 were analyzed. Patients were classified into three groups according to the diagnostic process: those diagnosed intraoperatively without prior imaging (Group 1), those who underwent imaging but were diagnosed intraoperatively (Group 2), and those diagnosed preoperatively by computed tomography (CT) (Group 3). Demographic characteristics, mechanisms of injury, surgical approaches, postoperative complications, and prognostic scores, including the Injury Severity Score (ISS) and Modified Shock Index (MSI), were evaluated. Results Most patients were male (97.6%), and the left hemidiaphragm was the most frequently injured side (63.4%). Penetrating trauma (68.2%) was more common than blunt trauma, with gunshot wounds (34.1%) and stab wounds (34.1%) representing the most common mechanisms of injury. Laparotomy was the most frequently performed surgical approach (41.5%), and primary repair was achieved in 92.5% of patients. The overall postoperative complication rate was 37.5%, with atelectasis being the most common complication (26.7%). ISS scores were significantly higher in patients diagnosed intraoperatively than in those diagnosed preoperatively by imaging (p<0.001). Patients who underwent surgery within the first two hours after admission had higher ISS scores than those who underwent delayed surgery (p<0.001). ISS scores were significantly higher among patients operated on by the General Surgery department than among those treated by the Thoracic Surgery department. In contrast, MSI scores were lower in Thoracic Surgery patients who underwent emergency surgery for hemothorax than in General Surgery patients. Conclusion TDI remains a diagnostically challenging condition, and early surgical intervention is crucial for reducing mortality. Despite advances in imaging techniques, some cases continue to be overlooked because of concomitant injuries. Therefore, a high index of clinical suspicion and close patient monitoring are essential for timely diagnosis. Furthermore, differences in ISS and MSI scores between patients managed by different surgical specialties may reflect variations in trauma severity, surgical decision-making, and timing of intervention.

title: Emergency management of obturator hernıa in elderly patients: A case series and surgical strategy.
abstract: Obturator hernia (OH) is a rare but potentially life-threatening cause of intestinal obstruction, accounting for approximately 0.07-1% of all abdominal wall hernias. It occurs predominantly in very elderly, multiparous, and underweight women and is commonly referred to as the 'little old lady's hernia.' Due to its deep anatomical location and the absence of specific clinical findings, OH remains a significant diagnostic challenge even for experienced surgeons. Diagnostic delay is common and contributes to the high reported mortality rates, ranging between 13% and 40%. Therefore, early recognition supported by a high index of clinical suspicion is essential for improving outcomes. Computed tomography (CT) has become the most reliable imaging modality for preoperative diagnosis, enabling accurate identification of the herniated bowel loop as well as evaluation of bowel viability and associated complications. In this study, we present three elderly, cachectic female patients admitted with signs and symptoms of mechanical intestinal obstruction who were diagnosed with OH using CT imaging and underwent emergency surgical treatment. Surgical management included both laparoscopic transabdominal preperitoneal repair and open midline laparotomy depending on intraoperative findings and patient condition. In all cases, primary suture repair of the obturator defect was preferred instead of polypropylene mesh reinforcement. This strategy was guided by the presence of enteric contamination, bowel perforation, suspected ischemia, or advanced patient frailty associated with increased risk of delayed complications related to polypropylene mesh material. This case series demonstrates that successful management depends primarily on early CT-based diagnosis, sustained clinical suspicion, and individualized surgical decision-making.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Coronary Artery Disease: From Detection to Precision Management.
abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide, yet the landscape is rapidly evolving as artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to its detection, diagnosis, and management. This review surveys the expanding role of AI across the full spectrum of CAD care. In screening, deep-learning electrocardiography and electronic health record-based digital markers enable earlier identification of clinically significant disease. In noninvasive imaging, AI-driven coronary computed tomography angiography automates calcium scoring, derives fractional flow reserve without invasive wires, and quantifies high-risk plaque features that predict incident adverse events. Within the cardiac catheterization laboratory, angiography-derived physiologic assessment and AI-guided intravascular imaging segmentation support real-time procedural decision-making. Beyond diagnosis, machine-learning models integrating multimodality imaging data improve risk stratification over conventional clinical scores, while pharmacogenomic algorithms and wearable-based digital rehabilitation platforms enable patient-centric secondary prevention. Despite this progress, significant challenges persist, including limited evidence from randomized trials, algorithmic bias in underrepresented populations, regulatory uncertainty surrounding software-as-a-medical-device frameworks, and the risk of clinician de-skilling. AI has the potential to act as a collaborative tool that augments-rather than replaces-physician judgment. Future directions include foundation models, multiomics integration, agentic AI workflows, and equity-centered deployment strategies to ensure that AI-driven advances benefit all individuals with CAD.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Valvular Heart Disease: Imaging, Quantification, Risk Prediction, and Potential Clinical Decision Support.
abstract: Valvular heart disease (VHD) affects a substantial proportion of the population and remains a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality worldwide. Despite advances in surgical and transcatheter therapies, important challenges persist. VHD remains underdiagnosed, assessment of disease severity is often variable, and the optimal timing of intervention continues to evolve. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool across the spectrum of VHD care. AI-based electrocardiogram analysis can identify both existing and future VHD, while AI-guided point-of-care ultrasound extends screening to nonspecialist settings. Across multimodality imaging, machine learning (ML) and deep learning algorithms enable automated, reproducible assessment of VHD. In echocardiography, AI supports grading of disease severity across the main valvular lesions, including Doppler interpretation and automated report generation. AI-enhanced cardiac magnetic resonance facilitates automated assessment of ventricular remodeling and myocardial fibrosis, while AI-assisted cardiac computed tomography improves procedural planning for transcatheter interventions. In parallel, ML has identified distinct patient phenotypes in multiple valvular lesions with differing clinical trajectories and responses to intervention. This review summarizes current applications of AI in detection, multimodality imaging, and potential clinical decision support for VHD and discusses opportunities and challenges for integration into routine practice.

title: RV-LV volumetric relationship during graded supine exercise in healthy adults assessed by cardiovascular magnetic resonance.
abstract: Exercise cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging (exCMR) enables quantitative assessment of biventricular responses during physiological stress. We aimed to characterize right ventricular (RV)-left ventricular (LV) volumetric relationships in healthy adults using exCMR. Eighteen healthy adults (9 males, 9 females) underwent exCMR. Electrocardiography-gated short-axis cine and phase-contrast flow images were obtained at rest, at a target heart rate of 100 beats/min (Ex1), and at 40% of peak work rate determined by cardiopulmonary exercise testing (Ex2). The RV-LV volumetric relationship was operationally represented by the RV/LV end-diastolic and end-systolic volume ratios derived from simultaneous cine volumetry. All participants completed the protocol, and all cine and phase-contrast datasets were analyzed. During exercise, stroke volume increased in both ventricles predominantly through a reduction in end-systolic volume (ESV), whereas end-diastolic volume (EDV) changed little. Cine-derived LV and RV stroke volumes showed internal concordance with phase-contrast flow-derived measurements. The RV/LV EDV ratio (1.03, 1.03, and 1.03 at rest, Ex1, and Ex2, respectively) and RV/LV ESV ratio (1.09, 1.09, and 1.08 at rest, Ex1, and Ex2, respectively) remained stable across stages. Healthy adults maintained a stable relative RV-LV volumetric relationship during low-to-moderate intensity supine exercise. These findings provide quantitative physiological reference data for future disease-focused studies.

title: Cross-spatial attention guided multi-scale fusion network for precise microaneurysm segmentation.
abstract: Objectives Accurate detection of Microaneurysms (MAs) is crucial for the early diagnosis of diabetic retinopathy (DR). However, due to their small size and low contrast with the background, precisely segmenting them from the background poses significant challenges. Methods The Cross-Spatial Attention Embedded Multi-Scale Fusion Network (CSAFNet) is proposed to enhance the segmentation accuracy of MAs in fundus images. Based on the U-Net architecture, an improved ResNet50 is used as the backbone for feature extraction. An Efficient Multi-scale Attention (EMA) module is embedded to capture key features across different spatial locations and scales. Simultaneously, a Multi-Scale Deep Fusion (MSDF) module is designed to integrate contextual features from multiple scales. Additionally, the proposed Balanced Focusing Boundary (BFB) loss function improves segmentation by enhancing geometric accuracy at object boundaries. Results The method is evaluated on four datasets (E-ophtha, TongjiU-DROD, IDRiD, Messidor) with various advanced methods. On IDRiD, its F1-score and IoU improved by 6.16 and 5.63 % respectively, compared to the state-of-the-art (SOTA). On the Messidor and TongjiU-DROD datasets, it demonstrated comprehensive superiority in sensitivity, specificity, F1-score, and IoU. Conclusions The proposed CSAFNet can accurately extract MAs from fundus images, thereby effectively assisting in the precise diagnosis of DR.

title: YOLOv11-based segmentation of vitiligo lesions using standardized clinical photography.
abstract: Objectives To develop and validate a YOLOv11-based deep learning framework that automatically segments vitiligo lesions in standardized clinical photographs captured under controlled conditions, enabling reproducible lesion quantification across longitudinal visits. Methods Standardized photographs from 18 patients were acquired at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months under controlled imaging conditions, including fixed lighting, camera settings, and color calibration. Images underwent preprocessing involving resizing, color and illumination normalization, noise reduction, and geometric standardization. Expert dermatologists generated binary lesion masks that were used as ground truth for training a one-stage YOLOv11 segmentation model. Model performance was evaluated using patient-wise data splits and 5-fold cross-validation. Results The proposed model achieved 95 % accuracy, 92 % precision, 89 % recall, 90 % F1-score, with mAP@0.5 values of 0.878 (bounding box) and 0.892 (mask) from precision-recall analysis. Qualitative review indicated consistent segmentation quality across follow-up visits and moderate illumination variations, though formally stratified quantitative analysis by visit was not performed in this study. Visual assessment demonstrated close agreement between predicted and expert-annotated lesion boundaries, with minor under-segmentation observed mainly in low-contrast peripheral regions. Conclusions Standardized clinical photography combined with a YOLOv11-based segmentation framework enables reliable vitiligo lesion delineation and has potential for integration into quantitative disease monitoring and clinical decision-support systems.

title: Cervical lymph node image analysis using YOLO11 segmentation model: an application and performance study.
abstract: Objectives Ultrasound assessment of superficial cervical lymph nodes is clinically valuable, yet current diagnostic methods are highly operator-dependent, with limited objectivity and consistency. This study investigates a more objective approach for analyzing lymph node ultrasound images, focusing on the stability and practical applicability of different model architectures on real-world clinical data. It aims to evaluate the utility of deep learning models for detection and segmentation of superficial lymph nodes and to provide a feasible methodology for objective lymph node ultrasound analysis. Methods Using real-world clinical data, a cervical lymph node ultrasound image dataset comprising 1,050 patients was constructed, with histopathological confirmation and standardized clinical-imaging follow-up (≥50 % diameter reduction over 6-9 months after treatment) serving as reference standards. Three different models - transformer-based RF-DETR, two-stage YOLO11+MedSAM, and end-to-end YOLO11-Seg - were systematically compared on detection and segmentation tasks within the same dataset. Results YOLO11-Seg demonstrated superior performance in both detection and segmentation. Under COCO evaluation metrics, it achieved an mean average precision (mAP) at 0.5 of 0.795 and an mAP at 0.5:0.95 of 0.558. Pixel-level segmentation evaluation yielded a Dice coefficient of 0.775 ± 0.15 and an IoU of 0.645 ± 0.15, with Precision and Recall values of 0.796 and 0.783, respectively. In contrast, the two-stage YOLO11+MedSAM and Transformer-based models exhibited lower accuracy and reduced consistency. Conclusions This study provides preliminary evidence for the application of deep learning-based methods in lymph node ultrasound analysis and suggests a potential technical framework for generating structured imaging data, which may support future computer-assisted assessment pending further validation.

title: Current findings, application, and diagnosis of magnetic resonance imaging in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a heterogeneous neurodegenerative disorder within the motor neuron disease (MND) spectrum, characterized by progressive degeneration of upper and lower motor neurons. The clinical phenotype ranges from pure motor syndromes to forms with cognitive and behavioral impairment, and the pathological burden extends beyond the motor system. Diagnosis remains primarily clinical, supported by electrophysiology and exclusion of mimics. Therefore, objective imaging biomarkers are urgently needed. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is widely used as an auxiliary and differential diagnostic tool in ALS. T1- and T2-weighted imaging can assess cortical thickness, gray matter atrophy, and signal changes. Diffusion tensor imaging probes white matter microstructure. Magnetic resonance spectroscopy detects neurochemical alterations. Resting-state functional MRI assesses functional connectivity and network organization. Susceptibility-weighted imaging is sensitive to iron and calcium deposition. Ultra-high-field MRI provides higher resolution and improved metabolite quantification. This critical review summarizes current findings on MRI in ALS, but importantly organizes the evidence by the specific question being addressed: pathological/histological correlates, diagnostic or discriminatory performance, and clinical associations with phenotype, severity, progression, and prognosis. We also discuss major limitations, including methodological heterogeneity, limited standardization, small and clinically heterogeneous cohorts, frequent use of healthy rather than disease controls, and scarce multicenter validation. Although advanced MRI has revealed robust group-level alterations, none of these techniques has yet become established in routine clinical diagnosis of ALS. We, therefore, distinguish promising research findings from validated clinical biomarkers and outline priorities for future translation.

title: Correlating Diffusion Tensor Imaging Metrics with Endocrine Subtypes in Pituitary Adenomas: Redefining Invasive Biological Behavior.
abstract: Pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs) exhibit significant biological heterogeneity, making accurate preoperative assessment of their invasive behavior a critical clinical challenge. Traditional anatomic criteria, such as the Knosp grading system, fail to capture the underlying microscopic processes that define true biological aggressiveness. This review explores the emerging role of diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) in correlating microstructural metrics-specifically fractional anisotropy and mean diffusivity-with distinct endocrine subtypes (growth hormone-secreting, adrenocorticotropic hormone-secreting, prolactin-secreting, and nonfunctioning PitNETs). We synthesize evidence demonstrating that DTI parameters reflect key pathological features, such as fibrous content and cellular density, which are fundamental to tumor biology. Beyond subtype correlation, we examine the potential of DTI to serve as a noninvasive biomarker for predicting cavernous sinus invasion, visual pathway compromise, and tumor consistency, thereby proposing a paradigm shift from a purely anatomical to a functionally informed, "biological" definition of invasiveness. The review also critically addresses the technical challenges of DTI application in the sellar region, including standardization issues, the impact of tumor heterogeneity, and the limitations of current study designs. Finally, we envision a future multidimensional framework that integrates DTI with advanced magnetic resonance imaging techniques, radiomics, and molecular data to guide personalized surgical, pharmacological, and radiotherapeutic strategies, ultimately aiming to improve patient prognostication and management outcomes.

title: Revisiting the Role of Chemotherapy in Advanced Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma: A Case Report and Review of the Literature.
abstract: Background Chemotherapy has been always considered scarcely or completely ineffective in the treatment of metastatic and progressive MTC. Case report We report the case of a 45-year-old man who underwent total thyroidectomy and lymphadenectomy in May 2023 for bilateral MTC with extrathyroidal extension and 2/23 metastatic lymph nodes. Germline and somatic RET genetic analysis were negative. From July 2023 to February 2024 tumour markers progressively increased and a 18F-DOPA PET/CT revealed metastases in the cervical region and mediastinal inlet. Therefore, cabozantinib was started, obtaining a partial response, but after 1 year of treatment disease progression at the cervicomediastinal level was documented, despite dosage increase. Thus, an off-label treatment with lenvatinib was started, achieving a transient stabilization. In October 2025, a further disease progression was diagnosed. The patient started off-label chemotherapy consisting of 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) 400 mg/m2 intravenous (IV) bolus, followed by 5-FU 2400 mg/m2 as a 48-hour infusion, combined with dacarbazine 800 mg/m2 IV in 30 minutes, every 14 days for the first month and then every 21 days for the following months. Chemotherapy was very well tolerated. At the last visit, after 17 cycles, tumour markers returned to the normal range (CA 19-9 22.9 kU/L, CEA 2.5 μg/L) and PET/CT scanning showed a complete response. Conclusion In conclusion, this case shows that, although treatment with multikinase inhibitors is actually the first choice for advanced RET-wild-type MTC, conventional chemotherapy can be effective at least in some patients and should always be considered, especially in case of failure of other approaches.

Background

Chemotherapy has been always considered scarcely or completely ineffective in the treatment of metastatic and progressive MTC.

Case report

We report the case of a 45-year-old man who underwent total thyroidectomy and lymphadenectomy in May 2023 for bilateral MTC with extrathyroidal extension and 2/23 metastatic lymph nodes. Germline and somatic RET genetic analysis were negative. From July 2023 to February 2024 tumour markers progressively increased and a 18F-DOPA PET/CT revealed metastases in the cervical region and mediastinal inlet. Therefore, cabozantinib was started, obtaining a partial response, but after 1 year of treatment disease progression at the cervicomediastinal level was documented, despite dosage increase. Thus, an off-label treatment with lenvatinib was started, achieving a transient stabilization. In October 2025, a further disease progression was diagnosed. The patient started off-label chemotherapy consisting of 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) 400 mg/m2 intravenous (IV) bolus, followed by 5-FU 2400 mg/m2 as a 48-hour infusion, combined with dacarbazine 800 mg/m2 IV in 30 minutes, every 14 days for the first month and then every 21 days for the following months. Chemotherapy was very well tolerated. At the last visit, after 17 cycles, tumour markers returned to the normal range (CA 19-9 22.9 kU/L, CEA 2.5 μg/L) and PET/CT scanning showed a complete response.

Conclusion

In conclusion, this case shows that, although treatment with multikinase inhibitors is actually the first choice for advanced RET-wild-type MTC, conventional chemotherapy can be effective at least in some patients and should always be considered, especially in case of failure of other approaches.

title: Whole-Lung Computed Tomography Radiomics-Based Machine Learning Classification of Nontuberculous Mycobacterial Lung Disease Across Geographically Distinct Cohorts.
abstract: Nontuberculous mycobacterial lung disease (NTM-LD) is highly heterogeneous, geographically and etiologically, hindering effective timely identification. Prior CT radiomics studies require manual segmentation of pathology. We developed a whole-lung CT radiomics-based machine learning approach and identified common features across two geographically distinct NTM-LD cohorts. We included 1,300 chest CT scans from China (871 TB; 429 NTM, Dataset 1) and 173 independent NTM cohort from the University of Alabama at Birmingham (UAB), US. Whole-lung regions were automatically segmented on each scan, and 85 quantitative radiomic features were extracted using a standardized image-processing pipeline. We evaluated two frameworks to assess model performance and generalizability: (1) training on Dataset 1 with external validation on Dataset 2, and (2) training on the combined cohort. Linear discriminant analysis (LDA) was used as the primary classification method. Cross-cohort concordance analysis was performed to evaluate the reproducibility of radiomic features across datasets. In Scenario 1, the LDA classifier trained on Dataset 1 achieved an AUC of 0.79 (95% CI, 0.73-0.84) with high specificity (0.91). On the external UAB cohort, the model achieved an AUC of 0.94 (95% CI, 0.90-0.97). In Scenario 2, the combined cohort model achieved an AUC of 0.81 (95% CI, 0.76-0.85) with improved sensitivity (0.61) and precision (0.82). Feature importance analysis identified 16 features consistently ranked among the top 20 in both scenarios, predominantly texture-based descriptors reflecting distinct parenchymal patterns between mycobacterial species. In conclusion, whole-lung CT radiomics enables interpretable NTM-LD classification across geographically distinct populations without manual annotation. Suggesting population-independent parenchymal signatures of NTM-LD.

title: Prehospital Trauma Compendium: Prehospital Management of Pediatric Traumatic Out-of-Hospital Circulatory Arrest - A Joint Position Statement and Resource Document of NAEMSP, ACS-COT, ACEP, and AAP.
abstract: In 2014 the National Association of EMS Physicians (NAEMSP), American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma (ACS-COT), American College of Emergency Physicians (ACEP), and American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) published the first joint position statement discussing withholding and discontinuing resuscitation attempts for pediatric traumatic out-of-hospital circulatory arrest (TOHCA). Since then, the body of literature addressing pediatric TOHCA has evolved and evidence has grown that demonstrates the nearly uniformly poor prognosis of children who suffer circulatory arrest in the prehospital setting as a result of trauma. To support emergency medical services (EMS) clinicians in their approach to these high-acuity, low-frequency, and challenging cases, this project aimed to update guidance regarding decisions to withhold or discontinue resuscitation efforts for pediatric traumatic circulatory arrest. NAEMSP, ACEP, ACS-COT, and AAP recommend: EMS resuscitation of pediatric TOHCA should: ○ Prioritize prompt identification of patients who may benefit from transport to definitive care at trauma centers when safe and appropriate. On-scene resuscitation should be balanced against the potential benefit of transfer to a proximate trauma center.○ Emphasize the identification of reversible causes of traumatic circulatory arrest and timely use of clinically indicated life-saving interventions (LSIs) within the EMS clinician's scope of practice. These include: ▪ External hemorrhage control with direct pressure, wound packing, and tourniquets▪ Airway management using the least-invasive airway interventions required to achieve and maintain airway patency, oxygenation, and adequate ventilation.▪ Chest decompression if clinical concern for tension pneumothorax. Empirical bilateral decompression is not recommended in the absence of suspected thoracic trauma.▪ External chest compressions and ventilations have a larger role in pediatric TOHCA resuscitation than in adult TOHCA resuscitation, with children frequently having TOHCA secondary to head injury, hypoxia and other non-hemorrhagic mechanisms. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) should be provided when the cause of circulatory arrest is unclear.▪ Epinephrine is of lower priority than other LSIs.○ Consider point of care ultrasound (POCUS) to guide decisions to withhold or discontinue resuscitation efforts.Resuscitation attempts may be withheld in pediatric TOHCA patients with: ○ Injuries that are incompatible with life (eg, decapitation, hemi-corpectomy, incineration).○ Evidence of prolonged circulatory arrest (eg, rigor mortis, dependent lividity, decomposition).○ Advanced care planning documents that indicate Do Not Resuscitate (DNR)/ Do Not Attempt Resuscitation (DNAR)/Allow Natural Death medical orders.
