title: Beyond Classification Accuracy: A Stability-Driven and Explainable Multi-Stage Radiomics Framework for Breast Ultrasound Image Classification
abstract: Objective: The aim of this study is to reduce high-dimensional radiomic features extracted from breast ultrasound images into compact and stable subsets using a multi-stage feature selection process, and to evaluate the effectiveness of these features in classifying benign and malignant breast lesions through various machine learning algorithms. Methods: A total of 647 breast ultrasound images comprising 437 benign and 210 malignant cases obtained from the Breast Ultrasound Images (BUSI) dataset were used in this study. A total of 753 radiomic features were extracted using PyRadiomics, including first-order statistical, shape, and texture features, as well as features derived from wavelet and Laplacian of Gaussian transforms. To reduce feature dimensionality, a multi-stage feature selection approach was employed, consisting of variance filtering, correlation analysis, Mutual Information, Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO), and Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE). Compact radiomic feature sets comprising five and ten features—were evaluated using nine machine learning algorithms through three-, five-, and ten-fold stratified cross-validation. Final model performance was assessed using an 80% development and 20% hold-out test split. Classification performance was evaluated through bootstrap confidence intervals, DeLong and McNemar tests, as well as calibration and decision curve analyses. Feature selection stability and model explainability were investigated using selection frequency, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations), and permutation importance analyses. Results: As a result of a multi-stage feature selection process, compact candidate sets consisting of five and ten features were constructed. SVM and MLP models stood out due to their high classification performance. Explainability analyses, classification performance, and feature selection stability have provided significant opportunities for the multidimensional assessment of the diagnostic potential of compact radiomic feature sets. Conclusions: This study contributes to a comprehensive analysis of compact radiomics-based classification approaches by integrating explainability analyses, feature selection stability, statistical comparisons, and thorough model validation. For future research, validation using multi-center and independent datasets may be required to demonstrate clinical generalizability.

title: AI-Based Diagnosis of Alzheimer’s Disease Using Brain MRI: Can Artificial Intelligence Improve Early Detection and Diagnostic Accuracy?
abstract: Background: /Objectives: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a neurological disorder that adversely affects cognition, memory, and overall quality of life. Identifying AD in its initial phase is especially challenging when patients display cognitive impairments. Conventional methods rely on physicians to manually examine patients and analyze images, which is time-consuming and prone to errors. This review examines the use of artificial intelligence (AI) techniques for diagnosing AD using CT scans and MRI brain imaging. Methods: Research papers published from 2018 to 2026 were sourced from Google Scholar, IEEE Xplore, and Semantic Scholar. The techniques that were investigated in this study include Convolutional Neural Networks, 3D Convolutional Neural Networks, transfer learning, Vision Transformers, ensemble models, and multimodal approaches. Five research questions were posed to analyse the practicality of using AI-driven techniques in clinical settings, their novelty, scalability, robustness, and accuracy. Results: This study found that AI models can autonomously extract information from brain images and yield highly accurate results, with numerous researches demonstrating over 90% accuracy. Deep learning applied to MRI imaging is effective, while CT-based techniques can detect brain alterations when MRI is inaccessible. Different data types, including imaging, age, medical history, and vocal characteristics, can provide valuable insights into AD. However, issues remain, such as dataset discrepancies, variations among scanners and individuals, and insufficient testing of complex models on diverse populations. Conclusions: Future efforts should focus on accurate and transparent AI, integration of multiple data types, rapid and secure models, and testing on large datasets from multiple hospitals. AI should be developed to assist physicians in accurately diagnosing AD rather than replacing them.

title: Semantic Segmentation for Leaf-Level Severity Grading of Coffee Leaf Rust and American Leaf Spot on Flatbed Scans
abstract: Visual severity assessment of coffee leaf rust (Hemileia vastatrix) and American leaf spot (Mycena citricolor) is subjective. We trained DeepLabV3+, UNet++ and SegFormer-B5 per disease to segment lesions on flatbed scans of 684 detached Coffea arabica var. Esperanza L4A5 leaves (one site per disease; semi-automatic detector-plus-SAM 2 rust and hand-corrected leaf-spot masks) and graded severity (G0–G3). Under matched training (three seeds each), UNet++ and SegFormer-B5 were equivalent within post hoc margins in leaf-spot lesion intersection over union (IoU; 0.878 ± 0.004 vs. 0.888 ± 0.001) and mean absolute error; for rust (0.759 ± 0.015 vs. 0.769 ± 0.005), IoU equivalence held only with seeds averaged. DeepLabV3+ was lower. Against five experts, SegFormer-B5 agreed more closely than the average expert for leaf spot (quadratic-weighted kappa 0.88 vs. 0.80; Holm-adjusted p = 0.048 across ten model–panel contrasts) but not for rust. A validation-tuned color threshold, competitive for leaf spot, flagged 12 of 21 healthy leaves as rust (≥0.5%, abaxial face), the networks none; healthy leaves came only from the leaf-spot site. A validation-calibrated probability threshold reduced rust over-estimation relative to the reference (SegFormer-B5 bias +0.99 to +0.12 percentage points). On flatbed scans, a compact matched-trained UNet++ rivals SegFormer-B5; field photographs remain untested.

title: Postintubation Tracheal Lacerations Management: A Siet Position Paper
abstract: Background: Iatrogenic tracheal injuries are uncommon yet potentially life-threatening complications of airway management and thoracic interventions. Although awareness of post-intubation tracheal lacerations (PiTLs) has increased over recent decades, their management remains largely constructed on institutional experience, and standardized evidence-based recommendations are lacking. The Italian Society of Thoracic Endoscopy (SIET) therefore developed this position paper to provide practical guidance for the di-agnosis, classification, and management of PiTLs. Methods: A structured narrative review and expert consensus process were conducted to evaluate key diagnostic and therapeutic aspects of PiTL. PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus were searched from January 2000 through June 2026. Preliminary statements were de-veloped, reviewed, and refined through structured discussion by an 20-member panel of experts in thoracic surgery, interventional pulmonology, and anesthesiology. The re-sulting statements reflect the collective judgment of the expert panel and are intended as consensus-based recommendations within a position paper. Results: Flexible bronchoscopy remains the diagnostic gold standard to assess the precise location, length, depth, and circumferential involvement of the lesion. Management strategies are highly driven by physiological stability, ventilatory status, and morpho-logical characteristics, primarily using the Cardillo classification system. Conservative treatment is indicated for stable, spontaneously breathing patients (Cardillo Level I–II and selected IIIA), while early surgical intervention (within 24 hours) is recommended for severe cases with ventilatory instability or major complications (Cardillo Level IIIB–IV). Conclusions: PiTLs require early, comprehensive, and structured diagnostic evaluation, followed by individualized management. Adherence to the 17 SIET position statements provides a standardized framework for clinical decision-making and may help reduce variability in care.

Background:

Iatrogenic tracheal injuries are uncommon yet potentially life-threatening complications of airway management and thoracic interventions. Although awareness of post-intubation tracheal lacerations (PiTLs) has increased over recent decades, their management remains largely constructed on institutional experience, and standardized evidence-based recommendations are lacking. The Italian Society of Thoracic Endoscopy (SIET) therefore developed this position paper to provide practical guidance for the di-agnosis, classification, and management of PiTLs.

Methods:

A structured narrative review and expert consensus process were conducted to evaluate key diagnostic and therapeutic aspects of PiTL. PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus were searched from January 2000 through June 2026. Preliminary statements were de-veloped, reviewed, and refined through structured discussion by an 20-member panel of experts in thoracic surgery, interventional pulmonology, and anesthesiology. The re-sulting statements reflect the collective judgment of the expert panel and are intended as consensus-based recommendations within a position paper.

Results:

Flexible bronchoscopy remains the diagnostic gold standard to assess the precise location, length, depth, and circumferential involvement of the lesion. Management strategies are highly driven by physiological stability, ventilatory status, and morpho-logical characteristics, primarily using the Cardillo classification system. Conservative treatment is indicated for stable, spontaneously breathing patients (Cardillo Level I–II and selected IIIA), while early surgical intervention (within 24 hours) is recommended for severe cases with ventilatory instability or major complications (Cardillo Level IIIB–IV).

Conclusions:

PiTLs require early, comprehensive, and structured diagnostic evaluation, followed by individualized management. Adherence to the 17 SIET position statements provides a standardized framework for clinical decision-making and may help reduce variability in care.

title: Optimizing Deep Learning Pipelines for Retinopathy of Prematurity Classification: A Systematic Study from Preprocessing to Model Selection
abstract: Retinopathy of Prematurity (ROP) remains one of the leading causes of preventable childhood blindness, yet automated detection remains challenging due to variations in retinal fundus image quality, contrast, acquisition device characteristics, and disease representation, which proposes a deep learning pipeline for binary classification of healthy and ROP cases using the recently introduced ROPReLes dataset, which contains 6004 retinal images from188 subjects. To mitigate bias and prevent data leakage, a patient-wise data split was performed. Multiple preprocessing strategies were tested, including three normalization methods, contrast enhancement techniques (CLAHE & histogram equalization) and color-space transformations. Several data augmentation and class-balancing strategies were also evaluated, including weighted sampling, on-the-go augmentation, offline augmentation, and ratio-based augmentation. Performance was assessed using both baseline and state-of-the-art architectures, including a custom 2D convolutional neural network, ResNet18, Inception-v1, Inception-v3, EfficientNet, and Swin Transformer. The results show that model performance is strongly influenced by the combined effects of preprocessing, augmentation, class balancing, batch size, and model architecture. Ratio-based augmentation, applied only on the minority class, was the most effective class- balancing strategy. Among the evaluated models, Inception-v3 achieved the highest AUC (88.5%) and an accuracy of 91.3%. These findings highlight the importance of optimizing preprocessing, data balancing, and model selection as a unified pipeline for developing reliable automated ROP screening systems.

title: Augmented Reality and Virtual Reality in Thoracic Surgery: Current Applications and Objective Assessment of Surgical Competency—A Systematic Review
abstract: Background: /Objectives: Augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR) are increasingly utilized across the perioperative continuum in thoracic surgery. We performed a systematic review to elucidate the clinical utility of AR/VR technologies in general thoracic surgery, identify current technological trends, and evaluate their role as objective assessment tools for surgical competency. Methods: A comprehensive systematic search of the PubMed database was conducted from inception through 6 June 2026 in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Eligible peer-reviewed studies were categorized according to their clinical phase of utilization, perioperative surgical outcomes, and objective simulator-derived competency metrics. Results: A total of 1,013 records were initially identified, of which 74 met the inclusion criteria and were analyzed. Clinical applications of AR/VR in thoracic surgery spanned three principal domains: (1) surgical education and training, (2) preoperative anatomical planning and resection simulation, and (3) real-time intraoperative navigation (encompassing non-anatomical tumor localization and anatomical bronchovascular guidance). Integration of artificial intelligence (AI) further accelerated three-dimensional anatomical segmentation and intraoperative registration workflows. Across nine comparative cohort studies, AR/VR or three-dimensional guidance was associated with significantly shorter operative times in 77.8% (7/9) and lower estimated intraoperative blood loss in 55.6% (5/9) of studies without increasing postoperative complications. Furthermore, validated VR simulation platforms reliably stratified novice, intermediate, and experienced surgeons using automated kinematic metrics. Conclusions: AR and VR technologies enhance surgical training, complex segmentectomy planning, and intraoperative navigation. Standardized VR scoring systems incorporating procedural time, simulated blood loss, and instrument motion dynamics are warranted to advance objective surgical credentialing.

title: Prognostic Factors for Reoperation After Distal Femur Fracture Fixation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Background Distal femur fractures (DFFs) carry high rates of nonunion and reoperation despite decades of implant innovation, yet the factors driving these outcomes and the role of dual-implant constructs in high-risk settings remain poorly defined. The primary aim of this systematic review was to identify patient-, fracture-, and technical prognostic factors associated with reoperation for nonunion after DFF fixation; its secondary aim was to evaluate whether dual implant constructs demonstrated improved outcomes in adverse prognostic settings. Methods PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched through December 2025. Studies enrolling patients aged 16 years or older with DFFs, assessing single- or dual-implant constructs and at least 1 prognostic factor against a clinical or radiographic outcome, were included. Random-effects meta-analyses used unadjusted and adjusted odds ratios (aORs) for dichotomous outcomes, and standardized mean differences (SMDs) for continuous outcomes. Certainty of evidence was rated using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE). The primary outcome was reoperation for nonunion. Results A total of 121 studies (9,749 fractures) were included, with 18 contributing to meta-analysis. Four factors achieved moderate certainty of association with reoperation for nonunion: higher body mass index (BMI) (SMD 0.6, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.4-0.7), diabetes (aOR 2.3, 95% CI 0.8-6.0), open fracture (aOR 3.3, 95% CI 1.8-5.8), and stainless steel implant material (aOR 6.1, 95% CI 4.0-9.3). Preoperative infection (aOR 7.3, 95% CI 2.0-27.8) and medial bone gap greater than 1 cm (aOR 4.5, 95% CI 2.8-7.3) were associated with reoperation at low certainty. Most construct parameters showed no consistent independent associations, with technical factors appearing to matter most in the context of higher baseline fracture risk. Dual-implant constructs demonstrated superior outcomes in metaphyseal comminution and medial column deficiency, though no studies formally evaluated prognostic factors within these cohorts. Conclusions Open fracture, higher BMI, diabetes, and stainless steel material were the most consistently supported prognostic factors for reoperation, all at moderate certainty. Implant material is the only one of these directly modifiable by the surgeon; the remaining factors may represent candidate targets for dual-implant augmentation, pending confirmation in prognostic studies conducted within dual-implant cohorts. Technical construct parameters showed limited independent associations with reoperation; this likely reflects a floor effect of generally acceptable surgical quality, with their effects depending on clinical context, such as fracture severity or patient risk, rather than indicating these parameters are truly unimportant. Future research should prioritize prospective cohorts with harmonized variable definitions, prognostic analyses within dual implant cohorts, and reporting of all-cause reoperations. Level of evidence Prognostic Level III. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

title: Algorithm-based diagnosis and targeted epidural blood patch for spontaneous intracranial hypotension: a case report from a Vietnamese tertiary center
abstract: Abstract Background Spontaneous intracranial hypotension (SIH) is an increasingly recognized disorder caused by spinal cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leakage. Although characteristic brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings may suggest the diagnosis, precise localization of the leak often requires advanced imaging techniques. Reports describing the application of contemporary SIH diagnostic algorithms in Southeast Asia remain limited. Case presentation A 40-year-old Japanese woman presented with severe orthostatic headache and vertigo after heavy lifting and excessive neck rotation. Brain MRI demonstrated diffuse pachymeningeal enhancement, venous sinus engorgement, and brain sagging, yielding a Bern SIH score of 7 and indicating a high probability of spinal CSF leakage. Whole-spine MRI revealed a spinal longitudinal epidural CSF collection extending from T1 to T12. Based on the positive SLEC pattern, prone dynamic CT myelography was performed and identified a thoracic ventral dural tear at the T2 level. Targeted epidural blood patching was subsequently performed using 4 mL of autologous blood. Follow-up MRI demonstrated marked reduction of the epidural fluid collection and re-expansion of the thecal sac. The patient experienced gradual clinical improvement and was discharged with significant symptom relief. Conclusions This case illustrates the clinical value of a structured multimodality imaging approach for SIH, integrating the Bern SIH score, whole-spine MRI, and dynamic CT myelography to guide targeted treatment. Accurate leak localization enabled successful targeted epidural blood patching and favorable clinical recovery. Furthermore, this report demonstrates the feasibility of implementing advanced SIH diagnostic and interventional techniques in a Vietnamese tertiary-care hospital.

title: Sensitivity-oriented fusion of resting ECGs and structured CCTA reports for identifying angiography-defined severe right coronary artery stenosis: a single-centre retrospective study
abstract: Abstract Background: Failure to identify severe right coronary artery (RCA) stenosis may delay invasive assessment and treatment planning. Structured coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) reports provide anatomical screening information, but report-derived stenosis summaries do not capture electrophysiological consequences. We fused resting 12-lead electrocardiograms (ECGs) with structured CCTA report features in a multimodal model. We then evaluated sensitivity-oriented identification of RCA diameter stenosis of at least 70% in coronary angiography (CAG) reports. Results: This single-centre retrospective study included 1,904 ECG records from 760 patients who underwent ECG, CCTA, and CAG. CAG reports provided the reference labels. The model combined a one-dimensional residual network, axial multi-head self-attention, lead attention, and feature-wise linear modulation by report-derived stenosis features from four coronary arteries. Performance was estimated using internal patient-grouped fivefold cross-validation. At the patient level, the multimodal model achieved sensitivity of 0.849±0.037 and specificity of 0.690±0.037. Its area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.831±0.020, with accuracy of 0.764±0.028 and F1 score of 0.761±0.051. The structured-report model achieved an AUC of 0.794, sensitivity of 0.391, and specificity of 0.837. Thus, multimodal fusion increased sensitivity while reducing specificity. The ECG-only model achieved an AUC of 0.574. Ablation analyses associated CCTA fusion, temporal-decay weighting, and attention modules with internal performance. An ancillary post hoc analysis reclassified 38 of 66 CCTA false-positive patients as negative, but it did not establish clinical net benefit. Conclusions: In this selected single-centre cohort, ECG and structured CCTA report fusion produced a high-sensitivity operating profile for angiography-defined severe RCA stenosis, with a corresponding reduction in specificity. The model may warrant evaluation as a sensitivity-oriented secondary screening aid, but it cannot yet be used to rule out disease or claim prevention of missed diagnoses. Independent multicentre validation, prespecified threshold locking, calibration, and prospective clinical-utility assessment are required before implementation.

title: A Comparative Study of Advanced DCE Tracer Kinetic Models for IDH1 Genotyping and Progression-Free Survival Prediction in Gliomas
abstract: Abstract Objective To compare quantitative dynamic contrast-enhanced (qDCE)-MRI tracer kinetic models for differentiating IDH1 subtypes and to assess their value in predicting progression-free survival (PFS) in high-grade gliomas (HGGs). Materials and Methods This retrospective study analyzed preoperative qDCE-MRI from 80 patients with pathologically confirmed glioma. Quantitative parameters from TOFTS, EXTOFTS, ATH, BRIX, DP, and QTM models were computed. ROC analysis was used to assess IDH1 prediction. Cox proportional hazards regression was used to evaluate PFS prediction in 34 HGGs. Results The distributed parameter (DP) model’s cerebral blood volume (CBV) was the best single predictor of IDH1 status (AUC = 0.846). A combined model incorporating DP-CBV, QTM-derived fluid flow velocity, and tumor location achieved the highest diagnostic performance, with an apparent AUC of 0.909, a bootstrap .632 + AUC of 0.898, and a stratified 5-fold cross-validation AUC of 0.881 ± 0.011. The DP model’s permeability-surface area product (PS) was an independent predictor of poor PFS in HGG (HR = 2.22; P < 0.001). The prognostic model combining DP parameters and clinical factors had the highest apparent C-index (0.870), significantly outperforming a clinical-only model. Correlations were observed between key parameters (e.g., DP-CBV/PS) and angiogenesis/proliferation markers (VEGF, CD31, Ki-67; P < 0.05). Conclusion Advanced qDCE-MRI models, particularly the DP model, effectively distinguish IDH1 molecular subtypes and predict PFS in HGG. DP-CBV is the optimal single imaging biomarker for IDH1 genotyping, further enhanced by combining with QTM-u and tumor location. In the exploratory PFS analysis, DP-PS is an independent prognostic imaging marker for poor PFS. Integration of these qDCE-MRI parameters with clinical assessment may enhance diagnostic and prognostic stratification for personalized glioma management.

title: Transient Hiccups Persisting After Nerve Block with Compound Betamethasone: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Persistent hiccups are a rare adverse event of local glucocorticoid injection in interventional pain management, whereas most reported cases are attributed to systemic chemotherapy or steroid administration. Clinical evidence on hiccups secondary to compound betamethasone cervical sympathetic ganglion block, and their differential diagnosis in patients with gastrointestinal comorbidities, remains limited. We report two cases: Case 1 developed persistent hiccups within after cervical sympathetic ganglion block with compound betamethasone, lasting approximately 12 hours; Case 2 experienced symptom onset on the day after ultrasound-guided paravertebral nerve block with the same agent, normal electrolytes, no response to baclofen/acupuncture with the symptoms persisting for 7 days.

title: Histopathological alterations of deep cervical lymph nodes in Alzheimer's disease and their association with cognitive decline
abstract: Abstract Background Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is characterized by progressive cognitive and functional decline with amyloid-beta (Aβ) and tau pathology. In addition to abnormal protein aggregation, impaired clearance of brain-derived solutes through glymphatic and meningeal lymphatic pathways may contribute to disease progression. Deep cervical lymph nodes (DCLNs), as major downstream lymphoid structures of central nervous system drainage, may provide a peripheral histological window into the brain-cervical lymphatic axis. However, whether human DCLNs undergo histopathological remodeling in AD and whether such changes are clinically relevant remain unclear. Methods DCLNs were obtained from 66 participants, including 59 patients with moderate-to-severe AD and 7 cognitively unimpaired controls. Hematoxylin and eosin staining was used to assess lymph node morphology and germinal center (GC) abundance. Multiplex immunofluorescence was performed to evaluate Aβ, tau, alpha-smooth muscle actin (alpha-SMA), CD31, and LYVE-1. Cognitive and functional status were assessed using the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB), and Activities of Daily Living (ADL) scores. AD patients were stratified by GC abundance using a cutoff of 4 GCs. Multivariate logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic analysis, decision curve analysis, and 6-month postoperative follow-up were performed. Results DCLNs from patients with AD showed histopathological remodeling, including reduced GC abundance, structural disruption, fibrosis-related stromal changes, altered vascular and lymphatic marker expression, and detectable Aβ and tau immunoreactivity. Compared with patients with > 4 GCs, those with ≤ 4 GCs had worse baseline cognitive and functional status, including lower MMSE scores and higher CDR-SB and ADL scores. In multivariate analysis, higher alpha-SMA mean fluorescence intensity was associated with a lower likelihood of preserved GC abundance, whereas higher MMSE score was associated with preserved GC abundance. Patients with > 4 GCs also showed greater improvement in MMSE, CDR-SB, and ADL scores at 6 months postoperatively. Conclusions Human DCLNs exhibit histopathological remodeling in AD. Reduced GC abundance is associated with greater clinical impairment, fibrosis-related remodeling, and poorer 6-month postoperative improvement, suggesting that DCLN histopathology may have potential clinical and prognostic relevance in AD.

title: A Reproducible Microfluidic Platform Combined with Deep Learning Image Analysis Enables Quantitative Single-Cell Characterization of Keratinocyte Responses to Flow
abstract: Abstract Advanced in vitro models require physiologically relevant culture conditions together with objective and reproducible methods for quantitative cell analysis. Here, we present an integrated microfluidic tissue culture platform combining controlled recirculating flow with a Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) deep learning workflow for quantitative single-cell analysis of dense keratinocyte cultures. The platform comprises a custom 3D-printed microfluidic bioreactor with automated flow regulation and was experimentally validated for biocompatibility. Immortalized human keratinocytes (HaCaT) cultured under continuous flow ($50\,\mu\mathrm{L/min}$) were compared with static controls. Fluorescence microscopy images were analyzed using a computational pipeline based on Z-projections, spatial upsampling, and iterative HITL fine-tuning of the Cellpose (cyto3) model. The optimized workflow improved single-cell detection by more than $140\%$ compared with pretrained generalist segmentation models, enabling robust quantification of cell number, morphology, viability, and fluorescence marker expression in highly confluent cultures. Flow significantly increased metabolic activity, proliferation, cell area and diameter, and keratin 5 expression while preserving cell morphology. Under differentiation conditions, flow further enhanced keratin 10 (an early differentiation marker) expression while maintaining cell viability. title: Myxofibrosarcoma of the Mandible Curative Indent A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Introduction. Myxofibrosarcoma, previously termed the myxoid subtype of malignant fibrous histiocytoma, is a rare malignant neoplasm of the craniofacial skeleton, particularly the mandible. Its rarity results in limited data regarding clinical features, therapeutic approaches, and long-term outcomes. Patient Concerns. A 40-year-old male presented with a three-month history of a painless, progressively enlarging gingival mass in the right mandibular region, with ulceration in the gingivobuccal sulcus. Diagnosis. Panoramic radiography and FDG-PET/CT revealed a fluorodeoxyglucose-avid, ill-defined lytic lesion involving the right alveolar process with extension into the retromolar trigone, mandibular foramen, and mandibular canal. Incisional biopsy combined with histopathology and immunohistochemistry (vimentin +, CD31 +; CK-AE1/AE3, S-100, P63, HMB-45, desmin, synaptophysin negative; Ki-67 ~ 30%) confirmed high-grade epithelioid myxofibrosarcoma. Interventions. The patient underwent right hemimandibulectomy via a submandibular incision with a circumferential 2-cm surgical margin and reconstruction using a pectoralis major myocutaneous flap, followed by adjuvant chemotherapy and adjuvant radiotherapy (60 Gy in 30 fractions). Outcomes. Postoperative recovery was uneventful. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 7, transitioned to oral feeding by day 10, and remains disease-free at 20 months of follow-up. Conclusion. Mandibular MFS is extremely rare. Wide surgical resection with negative margins combined with multimodal adjuvant therapy and vigilant long-term follow-up remains the mainstay of curative management.

title: Teleophthalmology for preventable blindness screening in semi-urban primary care: a cost-effectiveness study from Brazil
abstract: Abstract Background Visual impairment from preventable causes remains a critical public health challenge in Brazil, where over 34% of the population has never undergone ophthalmic examination and specialist access is severely maldistributed. Diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, age-related macular degeneration, and cataract are leading causes of preventable blindness, yet systematic screening in primary care remains rare in semi-urban municipalities. This study evaluated the cost-effectiveness of a teleophthalmology-based active screening pathway versus the standard Brazilian Unified Health System (SUS) passive referral pathway, assessed acceptability among professionals and patients, and estimated quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) gained through early detection. Methods A multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted across eight Primary Health Care Units in a semi-urban municipality in Rio de Janeiro state, Brazil (October 2025–March 2026). A total of 1,290 patients aged 50 years or older and/or with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) were screened using a portable non-mydriatic fundus camera with remote specialist reporting assisted by artificial intelligence (AI)-based segmentation. A two-arm decision tree compared intervention costs (bottom-up micro-costing) against standard pathway costs (SIGTAP 2024/SISREG 2024) from the public payer perspective. The primary effectiveness measure was time to diagnosis. A QALY scenario analysis was performed using Brazilian-validated utility coefficients. Acceptability was assessed using the System Usability Scale (SUScale; n = 13 professionals) and the Telehealth Usability Questionnaire – Brazil (TUQ-Brazil; n = 99 patients). Results Of 1,290 patients, 41.79% had abnormal findings and 2.32% had ungradable images. Mean time to diagnosis was 1.26 days versus 83 days via standard referral. Cost per detected case was R$50.64 versus R$70.82, a reduction of 28.5%. Teleophthalmology was absolutely dominant across all sensitivity scenarios. A QALY analysis (n = 376) yielded an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) of –R$4,330/QALY, well below the SUS threshold (~ R$132,000/QALY). Professionals rated the platform 90.96 ± 5.91 (SUScale; “Excellent”). Patients reported a mean TUQ-Brazil score of 6.61 ± 0.32 out of 7.00, with 93.9% willing to reuse the service. Conclusions Teleophthalmology demonstrated absolute dominance over standard SUS referral in both cost-effectiveness and QALY analyses, delivering earlier diagnosis at lower cost. High bilateral acceptability supports scalability within the SUS, and these findings offer actionable evidence for policymakers considering portable fundus camera integration into semi-urban primary care networks.

title: Value of machine learning model based on superb microvascular imaging ultrasound radiomics in noninvasive assessment of chronic kidney disease
abstract: Abstract To noninvasively assess the chronicity of chronic kidney disease (CKD) using a machine learning (ML) model based on superb microvascular imaging (SMI) ultrasound radiomics, and to develop and validate a clinical-radiomics nomogram for individualized prediction. A total of 305 patients with CKD confirmed by renal biopsy were prospectively enrolled and divided into training (n = 213) and test (n = 92) cohorts. Radiomic features were extracted from SMI ultrasound images of the renal cortex. The most valuable features were selected using univariate analysis, Spearman correlation analysis, and the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) algorithm. Five ML algorithms—logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine, k-nearest neighbor, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost)—were trained and compared. A clinical-radiomics nomogram was constructed by integrating the radiomics score (Rad-score) with independent clinical predictors. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The XGBoost model demonstrated the best diagnostic performance among the five ML algorithms, with areas under the ROC curve (AUCs) of 0.903 and 0.888 in the training and test cohorts, respectively. Sex and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) were identified as independent clinical predictors. The combined clinical-radiomics nomogram, integrating the Rad-score with these clinical factors, showed excellent discrimination, with AUCs of 0.949 and 0.943 in the training and test cohorts, respectively. Calibration curves demonstrated good agreement between predicted and observed probabilities, and DCA confirmed the clinical utility of the nomogram. The ML classifier based on SMI ultrasound radiomics provides a promising noninvasive approach for assessing CKD chronicity. The nomogram combining SMI radiomic features with clinical characteristics offers clinicians comprehensive and personalized imaging information, which may facilitate individualized treatment decision-making.

title: Dual-center Development and External Validation of a Venous-phase CT Radiomics Model for Predicting PD-L1 Positivity in Non-small Cell Lung Cancer
abstract: Abstract Background: Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression is a clinically important biomarker for immunotherapy stratification in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, tissue-based assessment is limited by sampling bias and intratumoral heterogeneity. This study aimed to develop and externally validate a radiomics model based on venous-phase contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) for non-invasive prediction of PD-L1 positivity in NSCLC. Methods: A total of 259 patients with pathologically confirmed NSCLC from two institutions were retrospectively enrolled and divided into a training cohort (n = 135), an internal validation cohort (n = 50), and an independent external validation cohort (n = 74). Radiomics features were extracted from venous-phase CECT. After least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, selected features were used to construct XGBoost, random forest, and decision tree models. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration analysis, and decision curve analysis. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was performed to improve model interpretability. Results: Among 1,688 extracted radiomics features, two features were ultimately selected for model development. The XGBoost model showed favorable validation performance across cohorts, achieving AUCs of 0.838 (95% CI, 0.769–0.901), 0.801 (95% CI, 0.665–0.919), and 0.767 (95% CI, 0.650–0.873) in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. In the external validation cohort, the XGBoost model showed significantly better discrimination than the decision tree model while maintaining comparable performance to the random forest model. SHAP analysis demonstrated consistent feature contribution patterns across all cohorts. Conclusions: Venous-phase CECT radiomics enabled moderate but stable discrimination for predicting PD-L1 positivity in NSCLC across independent cohorts. The XGBoost model may serve as a non-invasive complementary decision-support tool for identifying patients with a higher likelihood of PD-L1 positivity.

title: Development and internal validation of a CSF-free machine-learning model to distinguish immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced encephalitis from HSV-1 and anti-LGI1 encephalitis
abstract: Abstract Background Immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced encephalitis (ICI-iE) is difficult to distinguish from herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) and anti-LGI1 encephalitis, and its work-up includes invasive cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) testing. We evaluated whether a model excluding CSF features could achieve discrimination similar to a CSF-inclusive model and support triage before lumbar puncture. Methods We reanalysed 51 complete cases (ICI-iE, 19; HSV-1, 20; anti-LGI1, 12) from a publicly available retrospective dataset combining registry-based ICI-iE cases with single-centre HSV-1 and anti-LGI1 comparators. Random-forest models with 29 features (including CSF) or 25 features (excluding CSF) were evaluated by repeated nested cross-validation (5 outer folds × 20 repeats). We assessed discrimination, calibration, decision curves, out-of-fold TreeSHAP values, and a hypothetical high-specificity rule-in strategy across assumed prevalences. Results Mean areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) across repeats were 0.894 with CSF and 0.902 without CSF. On the repeat-averaged out-of-fold predictions, AUCs were 0.911 with CSF and 0.908 without CSF, and an approximate DeLong comparison showed no significant difference (ΔAUC [with CSF minus without CSF], + 0.003; 95% CI, − 0.033 to + 0.040; p = 0.86). Encephalitis-typical magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings and C-reactive protein were the leading contributors. In an exploratory sensitivity analysis, additionally excluding MRI features from the CSF-free model yielded a mean cross-validated AUC of 0.769. At specificity of 0.967–0.973, sensitivity was 0.574–0.597. Under the hypothetical rule-in strategy, the true-positive classification proportion was 21%–22% at the cohort prevalence (37.3%) but 3%–6% at 5%–10% prevalence. False-positive classification remained 2–3% of patients across the evaluated prevalence scenarios. Calibration was poor. Conclusions In this small internally validated dataset, excluding CSF features did not materially lower the point estimate of discrimination, whereas discrimination depended substantially, but not exclusively, on MRI findings. The CSF-free model may support triage while confirmatory testing is pending but should not replace CSF testing to exclude HSV-1 encephalitis. External validation in standardised, representative cohorts is required, particularly given potential confounding by data source.

title: 3D Ischemic Stroke Lesion Segmentation in MRI with Attention U-Net and Voxel-Level Uncertainty Quantification
abstract: Abstract Ischemic stroke is a major cause of death and disability around the world, and accurate segmentation of stroke lesions from MRI diagnosis are critical for treatment planning and clinical decision making. Compared to traditional methods, while deep learning has advanced automated stroke segmentation, but existing approaches predict single binary masks with no estimate of prediction confidence, a crucial limitation since clinical usage would require knowledge on where the model can be trusted just as much as the prediction itself. We propose a reliability-aware 3D framework combining an Attention U-Net with Monte Carlo Dropout inference and an optimized decision threshold, tested on the ISLES 2022 benchmark (240 multi-center DWI + ADC cases; 168/36/36 split). At inference, T = 20 stochastic forward passes generate both a segmentation mask and a voxel-level uncertainty map. This work achieved a Dice of 0.6816 (IoU = 0.5526, Precision = 0.8764 and Recall = 0.6595) for single-model volumetric methods on this benchmark dataset, meanwhile boiling Monte Carlo Dropout increased Recall by + 2.65% at the zero-training cost. Uncertainty maps were semantically aligned but spatially localized to the edges of lesions, highly correlated with segmentation errors, and inversely associated with lesion size automatically marking small and difficult lesions as cases of high uncertainty.

title: Portable Spectrophotometric Olive Oil Quality Analysis System Integrated with Oxidative Stress-State Modeling
abstract: Abstract Olive oil quality control requires analytical methods that distinguishes authentic extra virgin olive oil from lower-grade or adulterated oils while simultaneously monitoring oxidation, phenolic depletion, and storage-related deterioration. Conventional reference techniques such as gas chromatography, liquid chromatography, nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, and standardized wet-chemistry assays remain essential for confirmatory analysis, yet their cost, infrastructure needs, and sample-processing demands limit continuous use at farms, mills, warehouses, and retail inspection points. Here we present a full research framework for a portable spectrophotometric olive oil quality analysis system that integrates ultraviolet-visible spectroscopy, near-infrared spectroscopy, chemometric calibration, edge-machine-learning classification, and oxidative stress-state modeling. The system is designed to quantify quality indicators such as free acidity, peroxide value, conjugated diene/triene absorbance, phenolic depletion, pigment degradation, and adulteration-associated spectral deviation without relying on destructive laboratory workflows. The research develops the platform as an analytical chemistry and embedded diagnostic system rather than as a simple consumer sensor. The designed instrument combines controlled optical illumination, wavelength-resolved detection, temperature-compensated sample handling, onboard preprocessing, encrypted data storage, and cloud-supported model governance. The biochemical model links spectral behavior to triglyceride structure, oleic-linoleic acid balance, phenolic antioxidant buffering, radical propagation, hydroperoxide accumulation, aldehyde formation, and the degradation of chlorophyll and carotenoid pigments during light or heat exposure. The computational model couples standard normal variate correction, derivative spectroscopy, principal component analysis, partial least squares regression, support vector machines, random forests, gradient boosting, and uncertainty-aware edge inference. A validation strategy is applied using authenticated extra virgin, virgin, refined, and pomace oils; controlled adulteration series with sunflower, soybean, canola, palm, and refined olive oils; and accelerated storage experiments under oxygen, heat, and light stress. Expected outputs include rapid screening of authenticity, estimation of regulatory quality parameters, early detection of oxidative instability, and generation of traceable reports for producers, inspectors, and supply-chain actors. The framework is aligned with international olive oil quality concepts while emphasizing that portable spectroscopy is best positioned as a high-throughput screening and decision-support layer rather than a replacement for legal confirmatory testing.

title: Transcript-based circulating tumor and cancer stem cell detection in inflammatory breast cancer: a six-year prospective evaluation of assay yield and prognostic performance
abstract: Abstract Inflammatory breast cancer (IBC) is a rare and aggressive presentation for which no validated blood-based monitoring tool exists, and the tumor emboli that define its biology have motivated interest in circulating tumor cell (CTC) assays. We prospectively evaluated a transcript-based platform combining epithelial CTC markers (MUC1, HER2, GA733-2) and cancer stem cell (CSC)-associated markers (TWIST, AKT, PI3K, ALDH1) in patients with stage III breast cancer enrolled from 2013 to 2020, comparing 54 patients with IBC against 23 with non-IBC disease across 222 quality-controlled serial samples. Using the manufacturer-defined positivity thresholds, 14% of samples were CTC-positive and 29% CSC-positive. No marker distinguished IBC from non-IBC at baseline: GA733-2 was positive in 7 of 54 IBC versus 1 of 23 non-IBC patients (p = 0.42), and the composite positive categories did not differ (p = 0.71 for CTC, p = 0.11 for CSC). HER2 and TWIST transcripts were undetectable at threshold in all 77 patients. Among 44 IBC patients evaluable for event-free survival over a median 65 months of follow-up, neither baseline CTC positivity (log-rank p = 0.10) nor CSC positivity (p = 0.55) stratified outcome. Threshold sensitivity analysis showed that detectable signal clustered an order of magnitude below the positivity cutoffs, so that no threshold produced both an adequate positivity rate and outcome discrimination. Positivity at any draw during follow-up, and an additive classification combining both marker classes, likewise showed no association with outcome. Benchmarked against a tumor-informed ctDNA assay evaluated by our group in the same disease setting, the two platforms showed near-identical sample-level positivity (29% versus 27%) and technical QC performance, yet only ctDNA positivity tracked disease trajectory and preceded radiographic relapse. These findings indicate that transcript-based CTC and CSC detection, as implemented here, does not provide clinically actionable risk stratification in IBC, and they support prioritizing sequencing-based circulating tumor DNA and next-generation CTC platforms for minimal residual disease monitoring in this population.

title: Impact of Body Mass Index Percentile on Ultrasound Diagnostic Performance and Operative Duration in Pediatric Appendicitis
abstract: Abstract Purpose Childhood obesity may affect diagnostic imaging and operative duration in pediatric appendicitis. We evaluated associations between body mass index (BMI) percentile, imaging outcomes, and operative duration. Methods We performed a retrospective cohort study of children younger than 18 years with surgically confirmed appendicitis presenting to a tertiary pediatric emergency department from 2010–2023. BMI percentiles were categorized using Centers for Disease Control and Prevention standards. Outcomes included computed tomography (CT) utilization, nondiagnostic ultrasound, and operative duration. Multivariable models adjusted for age, sex, and calendar year. Results Of 2,275 children, 2,011 had valid BMI classification. CT utilization did not differ across BMI categories (p = 0.143). Nondiagnostic ultrasound was more frequent in children with Overweight and Obesity, although categorical differences were not significant (p = 0.079). Increasing BMI percentile was independently associated with nondiagnostic ultrasound (aOR 1.07 per 10-percentile increase, 95% CI 1.02–1.13; p = 0.011) and longer operative duration (β = 0.69 minutes per 10-percentile increase, 95% CI 0.07–1.32; p = 0.030), but not CT utilization (p = 0.146). Conclusion Increasing BMI percentile was associated with nondiagnostic ultrasound and modestly longer operative duration, but not CT utilization.

title: Lesion-Grounded Content-Based Retrieval of CT Findings Using Foundation Model Patch Embeddings for Case Review
abstract: Abstract Background Computed tomography (CT) education benefits from prior examinations containing related localized findings. Whole-volume retrieval can be driven by global anatomy or unrelated findings, while database-specific retrieval models limit reuse. This study evaluates whether patch tokens from a frozen volumetric CT foundation encoder can support a reusable lesion-grounded retrieval framework without task-specific retrieval fine-tuning. Methods Spatial patch tokens were pooled into lesion representations linked to their parent examination, annotation, and source finding text. ReXGroundingCT served as the demonstration benchmark. The primary evaluation used FlexiCT-3D to search 14,359 reference lesions with 407 public-validation queries from 50 CT examinations. Exact masks, bounding boxes, and loose boxes tested sensitivity to query-region precision. Retrieval was evaluated against ontology-based relevance, analytic chance expectations, and annotation-informed descriptor controls. Results For exact-mask queries, exact-subcategory Recall@1 was 0.484, more than three times the analytic chance expectation of 0.154, while Recall@10 was 0.848 versus 0.729. Bounding-box and loose-box queries gave Recall@10 of 0.840 and 0.821, respectively, but less precise query regions lowered early-rank performance. Under both box policies, embedding retrieval outperformed the descriptor-only control. Conclusions A reusable lesion-retrieval layer can be built from frozen volumetric foundation features without task-specific retrieval training. The layer retains links to source finding text without using text for ranking and can organize compatible medical-image databases into lesion-centered ranked lists and localized review panels for educational case comparison.

title: Hybrid U-Net Model with Transformer-Enhanced Skip Connections for Abdominal Organ Segmentation in Laparoscopic Images
abstract: Abstract The organ Segmentation in surgical images plays a crucial role in computer-assisted diagnosis and robotic surgeries, yet it faces challenges like class imbalance, occlusions, and computational constraints. In order to overcome these challenges, we propose an architecture which uses asymmetric multi-scale transformer along with the attention-gated skip connections in U-Net Model to efficiently segment abdominal organs. Our proposed architecture allows efficient extraction of local features and modelling of global contexts. We also propose a hybrid loss function by combining Lovasz-Softmax loss and sparse categorical cross-entropy loss, which helps in overcoming class imbalance in the training process and improving performance on the minor classes. Our proposed method attains a mean precision of 0.9667, mean recall of 0.9432, mean dice of 0.9522, mean IoU of 0.9150, and mean HD95 of 0.4704 on all 13 classes of the CholecSeg8k dataset, which makes it better than the state-of-the-art techniques.

title: Dynamic digital radiography–derived low signal area ratio for assessing emphysema and associated pulmonary vascular changes in COPD
abstract: Abstract Emphysema in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) destroys alveolar walls together with the alveolar capillary bed, yet unenhanced computed tomography (CT) quantifies parenchymal change rather than perfusion. Dynamic digital radiography (DDR) generates perfusion-related maps from cardiac-synchronised changes in radiographic lung density without contrast material. In 40 prospectively enrolled patients with clinically stable COPD who underwent breath-hold DDR, inspiratory high-resolution CT and pulmonary function testing, we quantified a low signal area (LSA) ratio by histogram-based segmentation of DDR perfusion maps. The LSA ratio correlated with the percentage low attenuation volume at CT ( r s = 0.692), forced expiratory volume in 1 s ( r s = − 0.553) and diffusing capacity ( r s = − 0.436). Absolute pulmonary vessel volume showed no association with the LSA ratio, whereas vessel volume normalised to lung volume did ( r s = − 0.556); this association persisted after adjustment for emphysema extent (partial r = − 0.324) and for lung volume (partial r = − 0.517), although its confidence interval approached zero. When both CT measures were considered simultaneously, the LSA ratio was more strongly related to emphysema extent than to vessel volume. The LSA ratio therefore reflects emphysematous destruction predominantly, with an additional pulmonary vascular component that requires confirmation.

title: CT-Derived Leaflet Sizing Discrepancy Is Associated With Valve-Related Events After Aortic Valve Neocuspidization
abstract: Abstract Background Accurate leaflet sizing is essential for aortic valve neocuspidization (AVNeo), yet objective anatomical references for selecting leaflet size remain limited. We investigated whether the discrepancy between a patient-specific computed tomography (CT)-derived anatomical reference and intraoperatively selected leaflet size was associated with valve-related events after AVNeo and assessed the reproducibility of the CT-derived measurements. Methods We retrospectively investigated 32 consecutive patients who underwent AVNeo with preoperative ECG-gated CT. A CT-derived reference leaflet size was geometrically estimated from the intercommissural distance. Sizing discrepancy was defined as the difference between the CT-derived reference and intraoperatively selected leaflet size, with maximum Δ representing the largest discrepancy among the three cusps. Interobserver reproducibility was assessed using independent measurements by a radiologic technologist, an experienced cardiovascular surgeon, and a cardiovascular surgery trainee. Associations with valve-related events were assessed using Cox proportional hazards and receiver operating characteristic analyses, and interobserver reliability was evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients. Results During a median follow-up of 23 months, valve-related events occurred in eight patients. Greater maximum Δ was associated with valve-related events (hazard ratio, 1.39 per 1-mm increase; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.09–1.78; P = 0.004). Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analysis identified 4.9 mm as the optimal cutoff (area under the curve [AUC], 0.818; 95% CI, 0.647–0.989), and patients with maximum Δ ≥ 4.9 mm had lower valve-related event-free survival (log-rank P = 0.020). Interobserver reliability was moderate to good, with intraclass correlation coefficients of 0.726 (95% CI, 0.339–0.881), 0.703 (95% CI, 0.231–0.879), and 0.832 (95% CI, 0.516–0.932) for the right coronary, left coronary, and noncoronary cusps, respectively. Observer-specific AUCs for maximum Δ were 0.776 for the radiologic technologist, 0.818 for the experienced cardiovascular surgeon, and 0.667 for the cardiovascular surgery trainee. Conclusions Greater discrepancy between the CT-derived anatomical reference and intraoperatively selected leaflet size was associated with subsequent valve-related events after AVNeo. CT-derived measurements showed moderate-to-good interobserver reliability, although discriminatory performance varied among observers. These findings support further investigation of CT-derived anatomical sizing as a patient-specific reference for AVNeo, while highlighting the need for standardized measurement methods and external validation in larger cohorts. Clinical trial registration Not applicable. This study was a retrospective observational study and was not a clinical trial.

title: Development and Validation of an MRI-Based Nomogram for Risk Stratification of Anxiety in Parkinson’s Disease
abstract: Abstract Objective Anxiety, a common and disabling non-motor symptom of Parkinson’s disease (PD), highlights the clinical importance of early identification of PD with anxiety (PDA). This study aimed to develop and internally validate an nomogram that integrates routine clinical indicators and structural MRI radiomic features for early PDA risk stratification. Methods 139 PD patients were retrospectively enrolled and split into training (n = 97) and internal test (n = 42) sets at a 7:3 ratio. 21 clinical variables were collected, and 584 quantitative morphological features were extracted. Mann-Whitney U test, Spearman collinearity elimination and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression were used to select optimal imaging metrics to calculate a radiomics signature. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression identified independent clinical predictors. A clinical prediction model and an integrated clinical–radiomics nomogram were constructed, and assessed in terms of accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, F1-score, receiver-operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration plots and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results Elevated UPDRS-III score, cognitive impairment, higher levodopa-benserazide dosage, and 12 MRI features were independent PDA predictors. The combined nomogram outperformed the clinical-only model, achieving an AUC of 0.99, accuracy of 0.93, sensitivity of 1.00, specificity of 0.91 in the test set. Calibration curves confirmed favorable consistency between predicted and actual anxiety risk, while DCA demonstrated sustained net clinical benefit of the integrated nomogram across wide threshold ranges. Conclusion The visualizable clinical-radiomics nomogram enables accurate individualized PDA risk prediction. This non-invasive, bedside-accessible tool assists neurologists in early screening and stratified management of PDA.

title: Thermo-regulatory response of static and dynamic breast thermography as a biomarker of malignancy
abstract: Abstract This study assesses the diagnostic potential of static and dynamic infrared thermography by relating physiological vascular patterns to established indicators of breast malignancy. Mammography remains the principal global screening modality; however, its accuracy declines in women with dense breast tissue [1], and its high cost limits access in developing countries [2]. Although dynamic thermal imaging may improve lesion detection, its clinical implementation in developing settings is constrained by the opacity of artificial intelligence models and the limited availability of high-quality datasets [3]. This paper presents a physiology-based model intended to reduce reliance on extensive training data and thereby facilitate analysis in small patient cohorts. Earlier Virtual Wave Transformation approaches appear to capture dynamic thermal responses but struggle to differentiate metabolic heat from vascular signals. The present study combines dynamic thermal imaging with static infrared imaging. By exploiting the different temporal behaviors of these signals, the model may distinguish increased cancer-related metabolic activity from other thermal patterns. In contrast to black-box deep-learning systems and even explainable AI approaches, this algorithm provides a more interpretable mathematical alternative by decomposing thermal patterns and separating convective vascular heat transport from thermal conductive metabolic signals. Analysis of the temporal variation in each component's amplitude indicates a possible association with patient diagnosis. Whereas conventional AI methods generally require large databases and expensive clinical validation, such as MRI, this approach uses physiological parameters to obtain diagnostic information from smaller samples. This work is a limited pilot study focused on evaluating the mathematical methods; we did not perform detailed statistical analysis.

title: Explainable AI-Based Pulmonary Nodule Classification from Computed Tomography Images with an End-to-End Clinical Decision Support Interface
abstract: Abstract Early and accurate detection of pulmonary nodules in computed tomography (CT) imaging is critical for reducing lung cancer mortality. Although deep learning-based computer-aided detection (CAD) systems have demonstrated promis-ing diagnostic performance, their widespread clinical adoption has been impeded by two persistent limitations: the absence of visual explainability and the lack of deployable end-to-end interfaces that integrate prediction, explanation, and clinical workflow. This paper presents an explainable, end-to-end CAD system for pulmonary nodule classification that addresses both shortcomings. The proposed system employs a transfer-learned ResNet-50 architecture, fine-tuned on 2,372 balanced CT patches extracted from the publicly available LUNA16 dataset. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) is integrated into the inference pipeline to generate per-prediction heatmaps that visually localize the discriminative regions driv-ing each classification decision. The complete system is deployed as a production-grade web application featuring a FastAPI backend and a React frontend, complete with authentication and database persistence. On a held-out test set of 356 samples, the proposed system achieves an accuracy of 90.45%, precision of 90.91%, recall of 89.89%, F1 score of 90.40%, and an AUC-ROC of 0.9615. A confidence-based abstention mechanism returns an “Inconclusive” verdict for predictions below a 60% probability threshold, reducing the risk of unreliable automated decisions. Rather than claiming state-of-the-art raw accuracy, this work’s principal contribution is demonstrating that competitive classification performance, real-time visual explainability, and a fully deployed, browser-accessible clinical interface can be integrated into a single reproducible, open-source system, contributing a practical baseline for future hospital validation studies.

title: Multiparametric CEST MRI–Guided Intranasal Theranostic Liposomes for Quantitative Biodistribution and Response Prediction in Glioblastoma
abstract: Abstract Glioblastoma (GBM) treatment is limited by the blood-brain-barrier(BBB) and lack of non-invasive methods to track drug delivery and therapeutic response simultaneously. We developed a theranostic strategy utilizing multiparametric chemical exchange saturation transfer(CEST) MRI to guide the nose-to-brain delivery of mucus-penetrating liposomes encapsulating gemcitabine and iohexol(1:1; Gem/Ioh-Lipo). These multiple CEST contrast indicated drug-specific signals (gemcitabine 2.4 ppm, iohexol 4.3 ppm and liposome − 3.5 ppm), demonstrating that > 70% intranasal dose reached the frontal cortex from the olfactory bulb.Importantly, CEST at 4.3 ppm strongly correlated with tumor response(R² > 0.9), indicating the prognostic value of image-guidance. Another CEST contrast (APTw at 3.5 ppm) indicated the tumor response, intranasal Gem/Ioh-Lipo produced an 8.6-fold tumor volume reduction versus drug-free liposomes (P < 0.0001). Controls showed a 55.9% increase in APTw signal in tumor (P < 0.005), indicating increased cellularity and proliferating cells, which were absent in treated animals. This CEST MRI-guided theranostic strategy enables non-invasive, real-time quantification of drug biodistribution and therapeutic efficacy for GBM, enabling precise treatment evaluation.

title: Large asymptomatic gastric duplication cyst presenting as an indeterminate gastrohepatic cystic mass in an adult: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Adult gastric duplication cysts are rare, and their organ of origin can be difficult to determine preoperatively, particularly when large and predominantly exophytic. We report a large, asymptomatic cyst arising from the anterior gastric wall near the lesser curvature and protruding into the gastrohepatic space, whose gastric origin was indeterminate on computed tomography. Case presentation An asymptomatic 27-year-old Han Chinese woman was incidentally found to have an upper abdominal cystic lesion during evaluation at a weight-management clinic. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography showed an approximately 8-cm, well-circumscribed, nonenhancing cystic mass adjacent to the lesser curvature, but its organ of origin remained unclear. Laparoscopic exploration showed that the lesion arose from the anterior gastric wall near the lesser curvature, with a broad attachment measuring approximately 5 × 5 cm, and was separable from adjacent organs. The cyst ruptured unintentionally during dissection, releasing an estimated 300–400 mL of yellow fluid, which was immediately evacuated. Recovery was uneventful, and computed tomography at approximately 3 months showed no visible residual lesion or re-formed cystic cavity. Conclusions A large, predominantly exophytic gastric duplication cyst may remain asymptomatic and mimic an indeterminate cystic mass in the gastrohepatic region. When imaging is inconclusive, correlation of the operative anatomy with the histopathological findings may support the diagnosis. title: Machine learning implementation for host-based infectious disease diagnostics
abstract: Abstract Host-based diagnostics coupled with machine learning may support faster discrimination of infectious states and reduce unnecessary antimicrobial treatment. We reviewed recent studies that applied machine-learning methods to clinical patient data for pathogen detection, infection classification, or closely related host-response diagnosis. Eligible infection targets included bacterial and viral infections, bacterial-versus-viral classification, and syndrome-based presentations such as sepsis. Malaria was included when evaluated within a mixed febrile cohort. Searches were conducted of four literature databases spanning January 2020 through August 2025. Of 144 retrieved records, 51 passed an initial host-diagnostics screen and 21 articles met the final eligibility criteria. The included articles covered structured clinical variables, gene or molecular-expression measurements, medical imaging, physiological signals, and microscopy. For the quantitative model-class comparison, we extracted 54 evaluations belonging to four machine-learning classes: random forest (23), neural network (17), support vector machine (9), and logistic regression (5). Less frequently evaluated approaches, including gradient boosting, decision trees, naive Bayes, and k-nearest neighbors, were summarized descriptively. Model performance could not be compared directly because input modalities, cohort composition, preprocessing, validation strategies, hyperparameter selection, and reported endpoints varied substantially. Accuracy and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were the dominant performance measures. Among the 54 focal-class evaluations, 14 reported accuracy alone, 20 reported AUC alone, and 20 reported both. Only 16 evaluations reported additional measures such as sensitivity, specificity, F1 score, or Matthews correlation coefficient. Imaging studies generally favored neural-network approaches, whereas molecular-expression studies frequently used random forests. However, the evidence did not support a universally optimal model.

title: Quality Assurance of Brachytherapy Treatment Planning Based on Template, Classification, and Segmentation Methods
abstract: Abstract Background and purpose Accurate applicator reconstruction is essential for dose calculation in CT-based brachytherapy. Reconstruction errors—driven by limited CT slice thickness and metal artifacts—can produce clinically relevant dose deviations. We developed a fully automated quality assurance (QA) pipeline that combines deep learning classification and segmentation with high-resolution template registration to verify the geometric accuracy of planned source dwell positions. Materials and methods We retrospectively collected 3,702 treatment plans from 742 gynecological cancer patients. A lightweight 3D convolutional neural network classified applicators into five categories, and an nnU-Net (v2) model segmented the three channels of Fletcher applicators. High-resolution (0.6-mm) template centerlines were registered to 3-mm clinical CT images using a progressive weighted arc-segment Kabsch algorithm. Geometric consistency was quantified with point-to-curve Euclidean distances. Error-detection performance was assessed in a simulation study in which one randomly selected dwell position per plan was displaced by 1, 3, or 5 mm (50 plans per magnitude), with 50 error-free plans as controls. Results The classification model achieved 99.28% accuracy and a weighted F1 score of 0.99. The segmentation model yielded a mean Dice coefficient of 90.7% and a 95% Hausdorff distance of approximately 1 mm. Mean distances between auto-segmented centerlines and the registered template curve ranged from 0.39 to 0.70 mm; mean dwell-point-to-template distances were 0.34–0.51 mm. In the simulation study, specificity was 94.0%; sensitivity was 36.0% for 1-mm displacements and 100% for both 3-mm and 5-mm displacements. Conclusion The proposed pipeline enables automated, high-precision QA of brachytherapy dwell positions and reliably detects displacements of 3 mm or larger, providing an objective tool for clinical treatment-plan verification that mitigates thick-slice artifacts through high-resolution template registration.

title: Screening of Bacillus bacterial strains with capability of degrading T-2 toxin
abstract: Abstract T-2 toxin (T-2) is a toxic fungal metabolite mainly produced by Fusarium species that are known to contaminate food products worldwide, posing serious risks to public health and the economy. Effective control of this toxin is therefore a key objective in food safety. Recent efforts to manage T-2 contamination have focused on utilizing microbes, especially bacterial species from the Bacillus genus, as promising toxin degraders. This study evaluated the in vitro capacity of ten Bacillus strains (BC1–10) in degrading T-2. Three out of ten strains demonstrated T-2 degradation activity, with complete toxin removal achieved within 96 hours under standard culture condition. The major biotransformation product of T-2 was isolated by high-performance liquid chromatography and structurally characterized by nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy as HT-2 toxin. Toxicity assessment in kidney-derived HEK293T cells showed that HT-2 was less toxic than T-2, with EC 50 values of 12.8 and 1.8 nM, respectively. The findings supported the potential application of selected Bacillus strains as functional microbial additives to mitigate T-2 contamination and toxicity.

title: Characterizing the Spatiotemporal Boundaries of Functional Ultrasound for Brain Decoding
abstract: Abstract Functional ultrasound imaging (fUS) measures task-associated changes in cerebral blood volume (CBV) with fine spatial sampling and rapid acquisition, supporting functional mapping and brain-signal decoding. As an indirect measure of neural activity, fUS-CBV signals are shaped by neurovascular coupling and vascular dynamics, which influence the spatial and temporal stimulus information available for decoding. Consequently, the functional distinctions accessible in fUS-CBV signals require characterization under controlled experimental conditions. Here, controlled whisker stimulation in awake, head-fixed mice was used to characterize these decoding-relevant response properties. Whisker identity and number, stimulation duration, and inter-stimulus interval were systematically varied. All-whisker stimulation produced contralaterally dominant responses in the primary somatosensory barrel field and ventral posteromedial thalamic nucleus. Different whisker inputs were associated with distinguishable cortical response distributions, while stimulation involving more whiskers produced broader representative activation patterns. Across durations of 0.5–10 s, brief stimulation generated measurable stimulus-associated signals, and response magnitude, persistence, and spatial distribution varied with stimulus duration. For paired 2-s stimuli, trial-level separability was already high at the shortest tested 1-s gap, corresponding to a 3-s onset-to-onset spacing, and reached 100% at gaps of 3 s or longer. Building on the experimentally characterized spatiotemporal response properties of fUS-CBV signals, a proof-of-concept modeling and decoding framework was developed, comprising cross-animal spatial prediction, classification of short versus long stimulation from S1BF ΔCBV time courses with known stimulus onset, and modeling of paired-event separability. Together, the results show that fUS-CBV signals retain structured spatial and temporal information about controlled sensory input after neurovascular transformation. These measured response properties characterize the spatiotemporal boundaries within which neural activity can be reliably distinguished using fUS-CBV signals, providing constraints for the development of fUS-based decoding models and the design of stimulation paradigms suitable for reliable fUS decoding.

title: Input resolution and decoder design shape Transformer-based retinal lesion segmentation: a controlled multi-seed study with zero-shot external evaluation
abstract: Abstract Background: Input resolution is usually reported as apreprocessing setting in retinal lesion segmentation, yet downsamplingcompresses small lesion annotations far more than large ones. We asked howresolution, encoder family and decoder design jointly affect segmentation ofmicroaneurysms, haemorrhages, hard exudates and soft exudates, and how much ofan apparent architecture ranking survives testing. Because input size alsochanges token count, positional-embedding interpolation, window configurationand the memory plan, we estimate resolution-conditioned system performance, notan isolated effect of spatial resolution. Methods: Four ImageNet-pretrained Transformer systems (ViT-Small/16,CaiT-XS24, Swin-Tiny, SwinV2-CR-Tiny) were trained on the FGADR Seg-set at 224,384, 512 and 768 pixels with five seeds each, under one frozen image-disjointpartition, schedule and scoring pipeline. A shared-final-decoder control and afixed-budget GroupNorm U-Net reference completed a frozen base of 120 models,evaluated on a held-out FGADR cohort and by zero-shot transfer to IDRiD.Outcomes were pooled pixel-level AUPR and mean average precision overlesion-positive images. Systems were compared under seed-paired \((t)\)-tests and ahierarchical seed-and-image bootstrap with Holm correction, and by equivalencetesting at margins of 0.01, 0.02 and 0.03. Results: Between 224 and 768 pixels macro pooled AUPR rose for all foursystems on FGADR (0.0794--0.1614) and IDRiD (0.1198--0.2150), but notmonotonically: CaiT-XS24 peaked at 512 pixels, a decline absent on FGADR underpositive-image aggregation. Most multiplicity-adjusted evidence lay in the firststep of the range. Pairwise testing separated systems far more readily underevaluation-cohort than seed resampling; externally at 768 pixels the two agreedon none of ten pairs. The hierarchical systems were equivalent internally at512 pixels and above at margins of 0.02 and 0.03, but not 0.01. A shared decoderreversed the ViT-Small/16 versus SwinV2-CR-Tiny ordering in all four conditions(\((p_{\mathrm{Holm}}=0.004)\)), an encoder--decoder interaction. Macro calibrationerror fell in all eight Transformer conditions (sign test \((p=0.008)\)), andtraining cost per epoch rose 11- to 38-fold. Conclusions: The benefit of resolution is neither universal, nordecoder-independent, nor free, and part of it depends on how performance isaggregated over lesion-negative images. Resolution, encoder and decoder shouldbe chosen together and reported with calibration, aggregation and measuredcompute.
